segments.html: Your oath is a blade you can draw at will, but it also cuts you when you falter.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you learn this talent, you do not keep a Pride note in the ordinary sense. Instead, choose a Vow or Oath in clear, binding terms with the GM. It must point your will and drive toward a very specific path, cause, or duty: a hard road, a sacred burden, a revenge, a rescue, a restoration, or some other life that cannot be finished easily or safely. It cannot be something already achieved, something trivial, or a promise so broad that it can fit any deed. You are not claiming a trophy; you are swearing yourself to a struggle. Your Vow or Oath Pride is never lost if you apply it to a check that fails. You also choose one Anathema—a deed you may never willingly perform and the GM must agree to it. If you break that Anathema, you immediately lose your Pride. This is the only way you can lose your Pride.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Add a second Anathema that sharpens your code, that the GM must agree on. When a roll clearly upholds your Vow you may spend 1 WP to add a D8 Artifact Die.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You may now invoke your Pride twice per session, and one of those uses can empower an ally at no further than Near range who is actively pursuing or aiding you in your Vow. They roll your Pride die but you pay the cost and count the use. If you refuse a beneficial opportunity because it would break an Anathema once per session, regain 1 special WP that doesn't count to your limit (you cannot gain another special WP until you spend it).
  • ✦ RANK 4: Add a third Anathema that the GM must agree on. The GM may now set formal Goals tied to your Vow — short-term goals award you +2 XP when completed (and +1 XP to each ally who meaningfully helped), while long-term Goals award +4 XP to you and +2 XP to assisting allies. These Goals must be weighty challenges where you are the spearhead.

• ✦ RANK 4: Add a third Anathema that the GM must agree on. The GM may now set formal Goals tied to your Vow — short-term goals award you +2 XP when completed (and +1 XP to each ally who meaningfully helped), while long-term Goals award +4 XP to you and +2 XP to assisting allies. These Goals must be weighty challenges where you are the spearhead.

segments.html: • ✦ RANK 5: You can invoke Pride an additional time per session, and this use can only benefit yourself. Once per session, when you use Pride in direct service of a Goal, you also grant each assisting ally +1 die on their next roll until the end of their next turn and you regain 1 WP if the action succeeds.

segments.html: You measure success by the wounds you intercept.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend 1 WP (SLOW action) to tackle an enemy within SHORT range and knock them prone. If their Strength exceeds yours, they can roll MIGHT to stay standing. No effect on monsters.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Spend 1 WP (FAST action) to instantly swap places with an ally within NEAR range.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Spend 1 WP at any time to leap in front of an ally within NEAR range and absorb 1 point of incoming damage per WP. Armor applies separately to you and the ally.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Spend any amount of WP to project a bulwark and choose up to that many enemies within your reach. Each chosen foe suffers –2 dice on attacks against your allies (they can still strike you normally) as long as they begin their turn within your reach. The penalty lasts until you move out of reach, they do, or you become Broken.
  • ✦ RANK 5: When you use Rank 3 or Rank 4, the first WP you spend counts towards two Enemies as once, and each chosen foe suffers -3 dice on attacks.

segments.html: You shout courage into being even when terror drowns the crowd and steady hands begin to shake.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend a FAST action to rouse yourself and your allies. Gain a Valor pool equal to WP spent; each point of Valor can be spent to soak 1 point of Attribute damage from PUSHED rolls to attack or defend in combat. When you soak damage in that way, you do not get WP. The pool vanishes at the end of the encounter, or if you become Broken.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You may allow allies within NEAR range to spend your Valor to soak Attribute damage from PUSHED rolls. When they soak damage in that way, they do not get WP. If you or your allies spend Valor on a melee attack, the attack deals 1 additional damage.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Once per combat when you gain a Valor pool, gain +1 extra point. As long as you have Valor, you and nearby allies gain that many bonus dice (up to maximum of 5) against FEAR attacks.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When you or your allies spend at least one point of Valor on a PUSHED roll, they can PUSH that roll one additional time (only one extra PUSH per roll). Each time a melee attack is pushed, it deals +1 extra damage.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Once per combat when you gain a Valor pool, gain +2 extra points instead of +1. As long as you have Valor, nearby allies (but not their mounts or companions) do not flee when they become Broken by FEAR, unless you are also Broken by that same attack.

segments.html: Druids read the world’s breath—mending wounds, stirring tempests, donning hide and antler, and listening to the drone of countless insects. Each Path also unlocks spell ranks within its discipline (see Chapter 6).
You channel the patient pulse of the land into broken bodies.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can cast rank 1 Healing spells and sense intense physical pain with a touch.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Rank 2 spells become available. Spend a quiet minute with your hand on a wound to numb the pain for a few minutes; this harmless flourish lets fellow healers know you are an Adept of the Path of Healing.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Rank 3 spells become available. Prolonged focus tells you whether the target shoulders crushing stress, grief, or panic, even if they hide it well.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Rank 4 spells become available. You can mask wounds older than a day, appearing hale even while hurt.

segments.html: You read the weather as easily as ink on parchment.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can cast rank 1 Nature spells. Concentrate on a NEAR zone to sense if civilized folk disturbed it within the past week.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Rank 2 spells become available. With a minute of focus you can coax the weather into small displays—summon a gust, pause the rain, cue a distant thunderclap, or send a scent drifting—signaling to other wardens that you are an Adept of the Path of Nature.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Rank 3 spells become available. You no longer need a camp when resting in woods or dark woods (treated as 6- and 9-dice camps). Each outdoor rest foretells tomorrow’s weather; spend 1 WP per extra day of forecast (up to a week).

• ✦ RANK 1: You can cast rank 1 Shapeshifting spells. You may mimic familiar animal calls, and for 1 WP they become perfect.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Rank 2 spells become available. Spend 1 WP to alter small features—eyes, teeth, claws, ear shape—for up to an hour; showing this trick lets other shapeshifters know you are an Adept of the Path of Shifting Shapes.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Rank 3 spells become available. Concentration reveals another creature’s pain. Spend 2 WP to carry an animal musk for a turn; clothing keeps the scent for a day.

  • ✦ RANK 5: Rank 5 spells become available. Animals of your totem treat you as uncanny kin—still wary if they must be, but never dismissive.

segments.html: Your senses sharpen until even dreams seem loud.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can cast rank 1 Awareness spells and instantly notice when someone touches you or your gear (pickpockets need one extra ⚔️ to avoid that).
  • ✦ RANK 2: Rank 2 spells become available. By touching a creature for a minute you can heighten one sense for a turn (so long as it isn’t crippled by injury); offering this favor tells other seers you are an Adept of the Path of Sight.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Rank 3 spells become available. Firelight stretches your sight 10 meters farther into darkness.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Rank 4 spells become available. You wake the moment danger erupts nearby.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Rank 5 spells become available. You feel small tremors—quakes, massive footsteps, distant explosions—before anyone else notices.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can cast rank 1 Swarm spells and urge nearby insects to gather or scatter around you, though biters may still feed if they choose.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Rank 2 spells become available. With a whisper of focus you can link to a small swarm for a turn, reshaping its movement or formation; this link tells other Swarm Adepts you follow their path.

segments.html:

  • ✦ RANK 4: Rank 4 spells become available. Spend 1 WP to cocoon yourself inside the BLANKET OF INSECTS for a Quarter Day, gaining the comfort of a 5-dice camp while it stands watch with 6 dice of SCOUTING. Once the Quarter Day ends the blanket disperses unless you spend another WP.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Rank 5 spells become available. Spend 1 WP to order the BLANKET OF INSECTS to SCOUT, TRACK, or FORAGE for you (6 dice), or to wrap around you as armor (Armor Rating 3). Each point of damage it prevents drains 1 point of the blanket’s Strength; when it reaches zero the swarm disperses and reforms after 3 Days (2 in woods, 1 in swamp). While shielding you it cannot attack, DODGE, or PARRY, takes only 1 damage from targeted strikes, and double from area attacks.

segments.html: Steel-sure fighters perfect brutal disciplines that turn every heartbeat of battle to their advantage.
You train until the blade feels like bone and sinew.

• ✦ RANK 1: When a close combat attack hits, spend 1 WP to ignore the target’s armor or natural armor.
  • ✦ RANK 2: After you have spent all your actions in a round, spend 1 WP to make one additional close combat attack (max once per round).
  • ✦ RANK 3: Before your foe rolls armor, spend WP to add +1 damage per point.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Spend 1 WP to have your weapon count as both a blade and one other melee weapon type, letting multiple weapon talents apply.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Rank 4 now treats your weapon as every melee weapon type at once for the action.

segments.html: You turn every tendon and ligament into a weapon.

• ✦ RANK 1: After succeeding with SHOVE, GRAPPLE, or BREAK FREE, you may spend WP to add the same number of ⚔️. Decide after the roll; this applies only to unarmed maneuvers.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Your unarmed strikes deal +1 damage and count as LIGHT BLUNT weapons for parries and talents. Once per round you may spend 1 WP to PARRY unarmed even without a held weapon or shield (attacks that normally disallow parries such as most monster strikes still cannot be parried). Gain +2 on that parry if the incoming attack wields a HEAVY weapon.
  • ✦ RANK 3: When an unarmed attack hits, spend 1 WP to apply any one close-combat stunt (SHOVE, DISARM, GRAPPLE, or RELOCATE) using the ⚔️ result of the unarmed attack.
  • ✦ RANK 4: While GRAPPLING a foe, spend 1 WP at the start of a round to treat them as cover: ranged attacks against you suffer –2 dice, and attacks that miss you deal damage to the grappled target equal to number of 💀 rolled. When a GRAPPLED foe is Broken from damage from its allies, regain 1 WP.

segments.html: You read the battlefield as if it were a board game.

• ✦ RANK 1: During the first round of combat (unless surprised), spend 1 WP to shift your initiative segment by up to +2 or -2. You also gain +1 die on one melee attack against one enemy who will act after you that round. This rank still can’t be used against monsters.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Spend 1 WP to block your target from using PARRY or DODGE on your next attack.
  • ✦ RANK 3: When your PARRY shows more ⚔️ than the attack, you can spend 1 WP to convert each extra ⚔️ into that many points of damage that can’t be parried or dodged. RANK 1 can now be used against monsters, and you may shift your segment by up to +3 or -3, or keep your current segment unchanged when you roll initiative next round. You can use this once per combat.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When you BREAK a foe, you may spend 1 WP to take their initiative segment on the next round (or keep your own if it is higher). This cannot be used in combat with monsters. RANK 2 now blocks the opponent from using both PARRY and DODGE.

segments.html: You are the bulwark others shelter behind.

• ✦ RANK 1: When a friend within NEAR range is attacked, spend 1 WP to parry for them. If the parry succeeds, you may choose to take any remaining damage; otherwise the attack resolves against the original target.
  • ✦ RANK 2: When you successfully parry for an ally with RANK 1, you may immediately swap positions with them or pull them a meter behind you without disengaging or provoking attacks. You become engaged with the parried Enemy.
  • ✦ RANK 3: After you successfully parry an attacker within ARM'S LENGTH, you may spend 1 WP to bind them with your shield. Bound foes suffer –2 dice on all attacks and cannot move out of engagement until they spend a FAST action to break free (opposed MIGHT vs your STRENGTH), or you release the bind by moving or using your weapon or shield for an attack.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Once per round you may spend 1 WP and PARRY a physical monster attack even if it normally forbids parries. Your shield shatters from the force and your shield hand is stunned until the end of the next turn.

segments.html: Hunters survive by listening to the wind, reading every hoofprint, and striking before a foe even knows they were found.
Your bow answers as soon as you draw breath.

• ✦ RANK 1: When your ranged attack hits, spend 1 WP to ignore the target's armor or natural armor.
  • ✦ RANK 2: After you have spent all of your actions in a round, spend 1 WP to fire one extra prepared shot (maximum once per round).
  • ✦ RANK 3: When your ranged attack hits, you may spend WP before the target rolls armor to add +1 damage per point.

segments.html: You share the hunt with animals that treat your word like pack-law. This path is usually paired with the TAMER talent, which lets you teach companions tricks; without that training they respond based on instinct and simple cues. Each rank deepens the bond and widens the stable of creatures willing to bleed for you.

• ✦ RANK 1: Choose one Small companion such as a fox, hunting dog, hawk, or other scout. It trusts you enough to follow you and warn of danger. They do not engage in combat, will flee to a nearby distance, and grant you +1 die on SCOUTING or SURVIVAL rolls made in the terrain that matches the companion’s natural habitat (e.g., forests for foxes, hills for hawks, wetlands for otters).
  • ✦ RANK 2: Gain a second companion and unlock Medium predators—war hound, wolves, boars, lynxes—who view you as their pack leader. They hunt and fight beside you even when wounded and will not abandon you unless ordered to flee. Companions act in the lowest segment each round.

• ✦ RANK 3: You may replace one Medium beast with a flyer, swimmer, or burrower (eagle, raven, otter, badger). Companions now mirror your instincts in battle: they act in your segment each round.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Large apex beasts (bear, great stag, saber cat) accept you as kin. Once per Quarter Day you may spend 1 WP to share senses with a companion for a few minutes—seeing, hearing, or smelling what it perceives while it prowls ahead.
  • ✦ RANK 5: One non-demonic monster with animal cunning (basilisk, giant lizard, iron boar) recognizes you as its chosen handler. It will risk itself to save you and, if separated, will carve a path back unless magic or death intervenes. When you become Broken you can immediately spend 1 WP to send any companion into a protective frenzy: until you recover or the beast is Broken, it adds a D8 Artifact Die to attacks against the enemy that felled you, acts on your initiative even if you are unconscious, and may leap in front of further blows aimed at you.

• ✦ RANK 4: Large apex beasts (bear, great stag, saber cat) accept you as kin. Once per Quarter Day you may spend 1 WP to share senses with a companion for a few minutes—seeing, hearing, or smelling what it perceives while it prowls ahead.

• ✦ RANK 5: One non-demonic monster with animal cunning (basilisk, giant lizard, iron boar) recognizes you as its chosen handler. It will risk itself to save you and, if separated, will carve a path back unless magic or death intervenes. segments.html: Gaining access to a creature type doesn’t hand you a ready mount—you still need to find and befriend it. When exploring a hex, spend a Quarter Day to search for signs of a suitable beast. Roll HUNTING and gather a number of successes equal to the rank of the companion you seek. Once spotted, make an ANIMAL HANDLING roll with a difficulty equal to half the rank (rounded up) to earn its attention; on a success it will follow you from a distance, often wary and prone to leave on a failure. Finally, bond with it for a number of days equal to that rank, spending a Quarter Day each day to earn its trust with an ANIMAL
HANDLING roll each Quarter; two consecutive failures will cause a strife and the process of bonding must start anew. Once bonded, the animal becomes a Companion.
Only attempt to tame a Rank 5 monster in hexes where the GM has signaled its presence (tracks, lairs, rumors)—otherwise you will not find a viable target.
If a companion dies you can tame a replacement during downtime (see Chapter 7) without losing talent ranks.
You move through the woodland like a shadow among old trees. All benefits from this path apply only while you are in forest or deep forest terrain unless otherwise noted.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you FORAGE, HUNT, SCOUT wildlife, handle mounts, or LEAD THE WAY through a forest, you may spend 1 WP to automatically succeed (decide after a failed roll). You may also spend 1 WP to treat difficult forest ground as normal for one Quarter Day; if you do, allies hiking with you gain +1 die on an ENDURANCE roll to keep up.

If the DODGE succeeds you end the action behind cover; you cannot attack the same foe until you spend a FAST action to spring from cover, but that foe cannot target you in melee until they spend a MOVE action to face you.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When you attack in a forest while benefiting from natural cover (trees, brush, ridges) or higher ground, add a D8 Artifact Die to the attack roll. If the target is unaware of your presence, upgrade that die to a D10.

segments.html: You carve trails where cliffs try to deny passage. Benefits apply in steep rock hills, mountains, and high passes.

• ✦ RANK 1: When climbing or scrambling, spend 1 WP to automatically succeed and set a piton line. Allies following your line gain +1 die on their CLIMB rolls and ignore the first failed roll (they simply slip back). You may also spend 1 WP at the start of a Quarter Day to scout the slope and mark switchbacks; for the rest of the day your party gains +1 die on LEAD THE WAY rolls in that mountain hex.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Spend 1 WP at the start of a Quarter Day to run thin-air drills; everyone within NEAR range (including beasts) ignores altitude COLD penalties for that period and gains +1 die on ENDURANCE rolls against wind or chill. Alternatively, spend 1 WP before a climb to rig hauling harnesses so every ally treats their carried load as one step lighter for the Quarter Day; if someone slips, the rope team may roll CLIMB to arrest the fall without damage.

• ✦ RANK 3: While adjacent to a cliff or rope line, you may fight in melee as long as one hand and foot stay on the stone. Enemies without similar purchase suffer –2 dice on melee attacks against you. Once per round you may spend a FAST action to anchor yourself; until your next turn, shove or grapple attempts to knock you off suffer –2 dice and taking damage doesn’t force a CLIMB roll. You still suffer –2 dice on ranged attacks while clinging to the face.
  • ✦ RANK 4: While holding on a rope, when you declare a DODGE you swing away instead of dropping prone, but your trajectory is unpredictable. Before the start of your next turn, make a MOVE roll; on success you gain momentum dice to your next attack against a single enemy equal to the number of successes minus one and stop Swinging; on a failure you continue Swinging and cannot take attacks until the end of your turn unless you spend a SLOW action to stop Swinging. While Swinging, you cannot attack enemies with melee attacks, and you cannot be attacked by melee attacks unless the enemies are flying. You also suffer -2 dice penalty to attempts to resist being SHOVED or GRAPPLED and ranged attacks against you suffer -2 dice. You cannot continue CLIMBING unless you stop Swinging. This maneuver requires an anchored rope or handhold, which may be attacked while you are Swinging.

Choose a zone uphill from your foes; every enemy in the target zone suffers a 11-die attack (Blunt, ignores armor) and must pass an opposed MOVE vs AVALANCE successes or be knocked prone and fall into the avalanche. Allies in that zone can attempt MOVE to brace and take half damage; on a failure they take full falling damage. After the slide you and your party may immediately reposition one zone aside or downwards without spending actions, representing riding the debris.

• ✦ RANK 1: When sneaking in dim light or darkness, spend WP after rolling STEALTH to add the same number of ⚔️.
  • ✦ RANK 2: If you are beyond ARM'S LENGTH, spend a FAST action and 1 WP to slip up to one zone into cover and roll STEALTH vs SCOUTING (with one free ⚔️ and distance penalties as if preparing a SNEAK ATTACK). Success ends your round with you hidden.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Spend at least 2 WP to designate prey you can see or track. All attacks against it gain +1 per 2 WP spent (maximum +1 per attack) until it is Broken or you release it. You can follow the prey's trail for one full day per WP spent.
  • ✦ RANK 4: After a successful DODGE, spend 1 WP to add one ⚔️ even after seeing the roll.

segments.html: Minstrels salt every tale with power—mending spirits, twisting tempers, or shattering nerve with a single note.
Your hymn knits spirits back together.

• ✦ RANK 1: Help a Broken ally within SHORT range rise again. For each WP spent, they recover one point in the attribute that hit zero. You can also spend WP on a one-for-one basis to add ⚔️ to an ally's ENDURANCE roll; declare the slow action before seeing the roll.
  • ✦ RANK 2: A number of your allies, equal to the number of WP you spend and within SHORT range, each recover one point of damage to an attribute. You decide which attribute they all recover.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Spend any amount of WP to transfer that much WP to a comrade within LONG range. The half-elf talent PSYCHIC POWER cannot modify this.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When you use RANK 2, each ally can take a free FAST action to stand up from prone, or get a free non-standing DODGE until the start of their turn.

segments.html: You bend moods with a word and a smile. All uses below require that your audience can hear you and isn’t actively hostile. A given individual or crowd can only be affected once per day. When you plant an intention they must attempt it at the next reasonable opportunity or suffer Empathy damage equal to your successes; if that would Break them, fear or social pressure forces compliance anyway. You can never compel obvious self-harm or betrayal of their core interests. Failing a roll still spends the WP and leaves the target or group wary or skeptical (–1 die to further attempts unless your reputation meaningfully improves). This talent only affects Kin, not monsters.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend 1 WP to make an opposed MANIPULATION roll with +2 dice against a single listener. On success you shift their attitude one step toward helpful and may plant a simple intention such as “open the gate” or “mention my offer.”
  • ✦ RANK 2: Apply Rank 1 to up to WITS listeners with one roll if they all listen to you. Each who fails to resist treats the idea as their own plan for the day. If one knowingly takes the Empathy damage to refuse, the rest suffer –1 die should they later try to shrug off the same intention. A failed roll makes the entire group skeptical rather than hostile.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Spend 1 WP and roll PERFORMANCE to sway an entire crowd at a market, tavern, sermon, or council. If the crowd is unruly or already skeptical, treat it as a Challenging roll (requires at least two ⚔️). Success sets their mood for the next scene and turns your slogan, rumor, or watchword into gossip that spreads through the settlement for the rest of the day. On a mishap the rumor twists against you and the crowd turns wary.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Put your reputation on the line. Spend 1 WP to convert one point of Reputation in this settlement or group into a D8 Artifact Die when influencing your target. If the Artifact Die shows no successes, that Reputation point is lost and you cannot try this ability in the same settlement or group until you gain a point in Reputation in it.

segments.html: • ✦ RANK 5: Spend 1 WP to open parley with monsters, demons, or other non-Kin intelligences within SHORT range. Roll MANIPULATION (+2 dice); hostile monsters require a Challenging success, and demons need one additional success unless the parlay aligns with their interests. On success they shift two attitude steps toward neutral and must halt the current combat round to hear you out. For the rest of the scene you may treat them as eligible targets for Ranks 1–4 so long as you maintain line of sight and speak a language they understand. If you betray them or issue commands that would obviously doom their lair or brood, the effect ends and they gain +2 dice on their next attack against you. On a critical success (three ⚔️ or more), demons agree to one request of no more than a sentence before negotiations conclude.

  • ✦ RANK 2: As Rank 1, but you can cajole payment. Total silver equals WP spent plus one for each ⚔️ on your PERFORMANCE roll, limited by what the audience can afford. You may forfeit silver to plant instead a rumor or lower the crowd hostility by one step.

Monsters take no damage but ignore non-hostile actions until the song ends, at which point they recall everything clearly.

segments.html: You run your stall with rule of bone and bellows—if you can’t buy it, you cobble it.

• ✦ RANK 1: In a few minutes and with scavenged scraps you can jury-rig a weapon, tool, or armor piece. Each WP spent (max 3) grants 1 gear die or Armor Rating, but the item looks crude (–2 MANIPULATION when flaunted), can’t be repaired, and takes damage on any gear die that shows a ⚔️.
  • ✦ RANK 2: When repairing an item, spend 1 WP to ignore a missing tool or talent (2 WP if both are missing). If you already have what you need, you may spend WP after the roll to convert each point into a ⚔️.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Spend 1 WP and a Quarter Day to toughen a weapon, item, or armor. The next point of item damage it would suffer is ignored, after which you can reapply the care. Once per day, if you finish a paid repair or custom build for a client in a settlement (or caravan/guild) where you haven’t already done so since dawn, regain 1 WP; you must move to a different settlement or customer base before you can trigger this refund again.

segments.html: You maintain ledgers, caches, and caravan partners across the Ravenlands. Spending WP means settling a tab or calling in a favor—when something “arrives,” it is an item you already purchased and warehoused, delivered through your network. Goods routed to you in the wild are

travel-worn (muddy seals, chipped edges, no crafter’s mark) and count as personal kit—not presentable enough to resell. At Rank 2 you can establish a caravan at a trading post that trades up to 25 weight (it costs 2D6x10 silver to establish, minus 2D6 per WP spent a day of manual labor organizing it); it produces no wealth on its own and requires you to personally supervise deliveries.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend WP to arrange the delivery of a trade good worth up to 1 silver per point from your ledger. The GM decides how it reaches you in that hex (runner, mule, hidden stash). No HEAVY items at this rank.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Your ledgers can now cover standard weapons as well as trade goods up to 1D6 silver per WP spent. You may also create or replace a caravan cache to store and deliver wares; caravans remain idle unless you are present.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Each WP can free up to 2D6 silver worth of goods, and you can assign trusted factors to run your caravan in a new settlement without you being present. You live by margins and whispers, turning junk into silver and silver into secrets.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend 1 WP while buying gear to trim the price by one-fifth per point (max 4 WP, reducing the cost to one-fifth). After you spend the WP, you gain +1 die on the next MANIPULATION roll tied to securing that deal (haggling, convincing the shopkeep, etc.).
  • ✦ RANK 2: Spend 1 WP while appraising loot for an hour to know its true value (artifacts remain priceless). When selling, each WP boosts the payout by 25% (max 4 WP); the GM may cap spending in tiny settlements, but at least 1 WP usually works. After you spend the WP, you gain +1 die on the next MANIPULATION roll used to pitch that item or close the sale.

segments.html: You bargain with a smile sharp enough to cut armor.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend 1 WP while conversing to attune to cadence and posture. For the rest of the conversation the GM must tell you whether the person you speak with feels sincere or evasive (but not which part of a long sentence is false).
  • ✦ RANK 2: The same read now exposes intent. After using Rank 1 on someone, spend 1 WP to ask what they hope to gain from this exchange (coin, time, status, information). This doesn’t force honesty or reveal secrets, but it tells you the motive steering their words.

• ✦ RANK 3: When you succeed at MANIPULATION to buy, sell or sign contract, spend 1 WP to seal the bargain immediately. The target waives any counter-offer or further negotiations and would lose 1 point of Reputation if they break the deal first, or renege on their agreement. Once per day, if you seal a contract or truce in a settlement where you haven’t already gained this refund since dawn, regain 1 WP. Move to a new settlement or negotiating circle before earning it again.

If they choose to break it, you immediately gain +2 dice on your next MANIPULATION roll against them (or the watching audience, if you pivot to them).

Once per day, when you publicly declare the truth or falsehood of a rumor in a new settlement (MANIPULATION or PERFORMANCE roll with at least three ⚔️), you may mark that proclamation; when it sways a settlement or a faction’s stance, regain 1 WP. Only one proclamation may be marked at a time.

segments.html: You bark an order and riders move before the hoofbeats fade.

• ✦ RANK 1: As a FAST action, spend WP to let up to that many allies immediately perform one of the following as a FREE action (lowest initiative acts first): MOVE or DISENGAGE once, stand from PRONE, or ready a DODGE (they may trigger it later that round). Allies must hear and understand the command.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Rank 1 can now grant any FAST action. You also gain a FAST reaction: roll PERFORMANCE and spend WP to blunt a FEAR attack for allies within SHORT range, reducing its effect by one ⚔️ per WP. If you are also targeted, you take Empathy damage instead of Wits.
  • ✦ RANK 3: As Rank 1, but you may spend 1 WP per ally to grant an immediate melee attack as a rushed SLOW action (still one per ally, lowest initiative first). These rushed strikes suffer –2 dice and the ally cannot PARRY or DODGE until the start of their next turn as they expose themselves to strikes.

segments.html: Your loyal steed shares your heartbeat and refuses to leave you in the dust. These talents only apply to the mount you personally ride (pony, horse, boar, giant lizard, etc.), not to general animal companions.

• ✦ RANK 1: While mounted you may spend 1 WP to bolster your steed. You ignore the first attempt at forced dismount (unless the mount is Broken) and grant the steed +1 die on opposed WITS roll to oppose FEAR checks for one turn, or until you dismount. If you become Broken while riding, the mount automatically withdraws to cover instead of bolting. If you spend 1 WP when you become Broken, your mount stays by your side and lashes out at anyone who tries to strike or move you.
  • ✦ RANK 2: When you act in a round, spend 1 WP to let your mount immediately take a close-combat action of its own (BITE or TRAMPLE attack, SHOVE, RELOCATE). This resolves after your action and does not benefit from your weapon talents, but counts as the mount’s attack for the round.
  • ✦ RANK 3: While you are on your mount, its BARDING ARMOR applies to your ARMOR against attacks you take: when you roll armor for that attack, add your mount’s barding Armor Rating to your own (the mount takes no damage unless the GM rules the blow clearly hit it). Outside combat you can spend 1 WP to let the mount KEEP WATCH while you REST in the saddle without forcing the mount to push on, and you can spend this Quarter Day to recover 1 point of Strength or Agility. You also gain +2 dice on ANIMAL HANDLING or HEALING rolls made to calm, spur, or heal your personal mount.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When separated from your mount, spend 1 WP to add a D12 artifact die (a Pride die based on your bond) to one roll made to reach it, provided you aren’t ignoring a simpler route. You cannot repeat this until you become in contact with your mount. As long as you are riding your mount, it cannot be Broken by FEAR attacks.

Later, spend 1 WP—even beyond DISTANT range—to trigger any number of these routines without further cues.

segments.html: Unlike Path of the Beast, these mounts are purpose-bred riding animals. You must still locate, purchase, or gentle them before the talent takes effect.

• Locate stock: Spend a Quarter Day searching the hex (or visit a trading post) for the desired stock. Roll ANIMAL HANDLING or SURVIVAL; accumulate a number of successes equal to the rank of mount you seek (see table). Donkeys, mules and ponies are bred and sold at trading posts. Riding herds are common near villages, rare in deep wilderness.
  • Approach/Break: Once you find a suitable animal, make an ANIMAL HANDLING roll with difficulty half the rank (rounded up). On a success it accepts tack and follows you; on a failure it bolts and you must start over.
  • Bond: Spend one Quarter Day per rank working the mount (brush, feed, tack). Each day roll ANIMAL HANDLING; two failures in a row spook it and you must begin anew. After bonding completes, the steed becomes your Companion mount.

You are a master at fighting mounted. All the effects of this talent require that you are mounted and in an OPEN zone in combat.

• ✦ RANK 1: While mounted, you may spend 1 WP to roll two extra dice on your initiative roll this round, keeping all successes. This can be combined with LIGHTNING FAST.
  • ✦ RANK 2: When mounted, you can spend WP to defend against attacks. Every WP eliminates one ⚔️ your enemy has rolled. You spend your WP before you roll for armor.
  • ✦ RANK 3: When you attack from a mount in close combat, and your attack roll succeeds, you can spend WP to increase damage. Every point spent increases the damage by one. You must state how many WP you use before your opponent rolls for armor.

segments.html: You and your steed devour leagues together. Benefits assume plains or rolling hills unless noted; in cramped terrain treat these as standard mounted travel.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend 1 WP to drive your mount one extra hex per Quarter Day across open plains (rolling hills count as difficult terrain and cost 2 WP per extra hex). Allies riding with you may attempt ANIMAL HANDLING; on a success they share the extra distance. You may also spend 1 WP while making camp to locate lush grazing and water—the party’s mounts and pack animals skip fodder consumption for the next Quarter Day.

segments.html:
• ✦ RANK 2: Spend 1 WP at sunrise to read winds and dust. The first LEAD THE WAY roll across plains that Quarter Day automatically succeeds, and all mounted allies gain +1 die on KEEP WATCH/SCOUTING while the omen lasts. Alternatively, spend 1 WP when breaking camp to launch a rolling column: the group mounts up without losing time, and allies gain +1 die on MOVE rolls to stay in formation during that Quarter Day.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Wedge Charge. Once per combat, if you begin at least one zone away and ride in a straight line to engage, add a D8 Artifact Die to your first mounted melee attack. Allied riders who launched from within NEAR range in the same round gain +1 die on their first mounted attack against targets in that zone.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Skirmish Screen. At the start of combat, declare you’ve fanned into a loose screen. While both you and one designated ally remain mounted and within NEAR range, melee attacks against either of you suffer –1 die and each of you gains +1 die if you attack the same target in the same turn (the bonus becomes +2 if that foe hits the other rider). The screen collapses if either rider dismounts or is Broken.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Once per encounter on open plains, spend 2 WP to direct a storm charge. Until the round ends, every mounted ally within SHORT range gains +1 die and +1 damage on attacks, enemies cannot PARRY attacks during this charge, and your mount may move one zone after each attack you make until the end of your turn, without spending extra actions. For this charge to provide benefits to your allies, each charging ally should move through the same zones as you do. If the coordinated charge Breaks or drives off at least one enemy, regain 1 WP.

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend 1 WP and a moment of prep to mimic someone of the same kin and sex. Anyone who knows them can roll INSIGHT at NEAR range to pierce the disguise; each extra WP spent imposes –1 on that roll.

  • ✦ RANK 4: While in disguise, add a D8 Artifact Die to STEALTH, MANIPULATION, and PERFORMANCE rolls.

segments.html: Every lunge is a question you already know the answer to.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can FEINT (FAST action, MANIPULATION vs INSIGHT) to bait the opponent into dropping their guard. On a success you may immediately spend up to 3 WP; each point adds +1 damage to your next melee attack against that target if it lands before the end of your next turn. The stored bonus is lost if you break engagement, fall prone, or attack someone else. Cannot target monsters.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Gain +1 die on the attack following a successful FEINT. You can also spend WP after the FEINT to reduce the target’s armor by 2 dice per point until their next turn (no effect on monsters).
  • ✦ RANK 3: If your last action was a FEINT, a successful PARRY lets you immediately COUNTERATTACK. Spend WP to add bonus dice or convert the counter into a SUNDER STRIKE. Rank 1 can now affect monsters.
  • ✦ RANK 4: After a successful FEINT you may DISENGAGE up to two meters within the same zone without provoking attacks, letting you re-engage elsewhere. Ranks 2 and 3 now work on monsters.
  • ✦ RANK 5: When your next attack after a FEINT hits, regain 1 WP per enemy within ENGAGED (these bonus WP expire at the end of your next turn). You may also spend 3 WP after a FEINT to make two attacks with one SLOW action. Gain the WP boon from each attack that hits.

On a success you may immediately spend up to 3 WP; each point adds +1 damage to your next melee attack against that target if it lands before the end of your next turn. The stored bonus is lost if you break engagement, fall prone, or attack someone else. Cannot target monsters.

• ✦ RANK 2: Gain +1 die on the attack following a successful FEINT. You can also spend WP after the FEINT to reduce the target’s armor by 2 dice per point until their next turn (no effect on monsters).

• ✦ RANK 3: If your last action was a FEINT, a successful PARRY lets you immediately COUNTERATTACK. Spend WP to add bonus dice or convert the counter into a SUNDER STRIKE. Rank 1 can now affect monsters.
• ✦ RANK 4: After a successful FEINT you may DISENGAGE up to two meters within the same zone without provoking attacks, letting you re-engage elsewhere. Ranks 2 and 3 now work on monsters.

• ✦ RANK 5: When your next attack after a FEINT hits, regain 1 WP per enemy within ENGAGED (these bonus WP expire at the end of your next turn). You may also spend 3 WP after a FEINT to make two attacks with one SLOW action. Gain the WP boon from each attack that hits.

segments.html: Some quarrels are settled in the square. Yours end in closets, alleys, and whispered apologies.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you land a SNEAK ATTACK with a LIGHT weapon (see Chapter 3 (Skills)), you may spend up to 3 WP; each point adds +1 damage if the blow connects.
  • ✦ RANK 2: After you successfully HIDE from a target, you can spend 1 WP to make a SNEAK ATTACK as a FAST action even if the mark knows you are nearby. You may hold that strike for later turns so long as you remain hidden.
  • ✦ RANK 3: When you hit someone with a LIGHT weapon while they are unaware, distracted, or tied up with another foe at ARM'S LENGTH, you may spend WP to press the advantage. Each point adds +1 damage and ignores armor entirely.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Spend 1 WP and a Day of legwork in a settlement, network, or stronghold to research a single target (or equally trained unit). Until a week passes, your attacks against that target deal +1 damage on a hit and rolls to shadow, infiltrate, or approach them gain +1 bonus die. You can maintain only one researched target at a time.
  • ✦ RANK 5: As Rank 4, but you may track up to a dozen targets, the research lasts for a month, and the related skill rolls gain +2 bonus dice.

segments.html: You travel with a pouch of tinctures and venoms, forever brewing something that smells of almonds or grave earth. Your reagent kit counts as one SMALL item that never encumbers you and can supply allies with doses that last up to four Quarter Days. Fresh poisons spoil too quickly to turn into trade goods unless the GM says otherwise. Monsters that lack explicit poison immunity suffer the listed effects; lethal toxins deal 1 Strength damage plus 1 more per full 10 HP
at the start of each of the victim’s turns. (Poison rules appear in Chapter 10 (Gear).)

• ✦ RANK 1: Spend 15 minutes and any number of WP to brew a lethal poison dose with Potency equal to WP × 3.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You may instead craft any poison described in Chapter 10 (Gear). Non-lethal brews gain +2 Potency dice.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can finish brewing with the poison already smeared on one weapon—no action required when you strike. You also gain +1 to ENDURANCE rolls against poison.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Any poison you apply gains +3 Potency dice and lingers on the weapon for one extra successful attack.
  • ✦ RANK 5: As Rank 4, but the coating endures for two extra attacks and your ENDURANCE bonus against poison rises to +2.

segments.html: If you lose the reagent kit, visit a trading post (or similar) to restock before using this path again—spend 1 WP and 2D6 silver to replace the supplies.
Your own vitae is spellbook, shield, and price. Each rank also unlocks the matching Blood Magic spells.

• ✦ RANK 1: Cast rank 1 Blood Magic spells. Your blood clots with uncanny speed, and any wound that failed to Break you leaves no scar once it heals.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Cast rank 2 spells. You can make fresh blood roil, pale, froth, or even coax a wound to bleed again for a moment; this display tells other Blood Adepts you walk their path.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Cast rank 3 spells. By concentrating and spending 1 WP you can halt severe bleeding that would otherwise demand ENDURANCE rolls (as long as that roll has no negative modifiers).
  • ✦ RANK 4: Cast rank 4 spells. Spend 1 WP to alter a sample of your blood so it imitates another kin. Trackers relying on spilled blood or scent need one extra ⚔️ to find you.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Cast rank 5 spells. Your body now replenishes blood through sheer will; you cannot bleed out, and by spending 2 WP you ignore all bleeding effects for up to a Day.

segments.html: You listen for the silence between heartbeats. Higher ranks open the corresponding Death Magic spells.

• ✦ RANK 1: Cast rank 1 Death Magic spells. You gain a death-sense, smelling rot or corpses out to VERY FAR range.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Cast rank 2 spells. You can make bodies twitch, skeletons clatter, or rot smell sweet for a moment; this macabre showmanship lets other necromancers know you share their path.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Cast rank 3 spells. You can eat carrion or spoiled meat without risk so long as the remains still possess structure (roughly less than a month old).
  • ✦ RANK 4: Cast rank 4 spells. Spend 1 WP to chill your body, cloud your skin, and pass as a freshly dead corpse—or even an UNDEAD—until someone pierces the ruse with INSIGHT.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Cast rank 5 spells. Spend 2 WP to enter a meditative coma that mimics death for a Day, extending it a further Day per additional WP. While in this trance you need no food or water, though you must still breathe if only barely.

• ✦ RANK 1: Cast rank 1 Symbolism spells. With a LORE roll you can read symbols left by other Symbolists, learning the spell used if your ⚔️ meet or exceed the effect’s rank.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Cast rank 2 spells. You can sketch harmless sigils that glow, sting with heat or cold, or stir a fleeting emotion; this flourish tells other Symbolists you are an Adept of their path.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Cast rank 3 spells. You may hide your symbols inside art, script, or fabric; spending 1 or 2 WP raises the SCOUTING requirement to 2 or 3 ⚔️ to detect them.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Cast rank 4 spells. Spend 2 WP to render your symbols invisible to everyone except Half-Elves and Symbolists of Rank 2 or higher.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Cast rank 5 spells. Spend 1 WP to shape a symbol purely within your mind as a FAST action, satisfying any spell that normally demands a drawn mark.

segments.html: Demonic mog seeps into you as you tinker with the unclean nature of demons. Each rank also unlocks the matching Demonic Magic spells.

• ✦ RANK 1: Cast rank 1 Demonic Magic spells. Your fingertips darken to a bruised lilac that never fades. Raw mog no longer burns your skin — you can handle it bare-handed, though it still corrodes your gear and harms anyone else who touches it.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Cast rank 2 spells. Lilac-green veins trace visibly up your arms and neck. The marks are involuntary — anyone who sees your bare skin can tell what you are. Other demon-workers recognize the stain on sight, and unbound demons hesitate one round before attacking you, studying you the way a wolf studies another wolf.

  • ✦ RANK 4: Cast rank 4 spells. Patches of your skin have gone hard and translucent. segments.html: Most ordinary folk cannot read and write beyond a few common words used in barter trade, but your community has retained the knowledge of the written word and has passed it to you. The Peddler profession begins play with Rank 1 of this talent for free (see Chapter 2).
Orc, Goblin, or Wolfkin detest the purpose of literacy; they cannot benefit from a tutor when training this skill.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can read and write in LANGUAGE (your kin). You are versed in trade measures and accounting and can apply them to the trade of a merchant using the MANIPULATION skill.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You can read and write in one additional language you have LANGUAGE talent at least Rank 1, except those learned outside your group (civilized or uncivilized), and those learned through the POLYGLOT talent.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You get the same effect as RANK 2, again. You also get +2 dice to attempt to decipher hidden meanings in texts, solve riddles, and try to grasp the concept of thieves' cant or other faction languages.

segments.html: Each spoken language in the Forbidden Lands is a separate talent. This talent does not give you the education to read or write written text, only to communicate verbally accompanied by body language if needed. When you create a character, you gain Rank 2 Language (your kin), and one Rank 1 Language (any other kin of the same group as your kin, civilized or uncivilized; such as dwarf for a human kin; or orc for a goblin kin). Half-kin (such as half-elves) may choose one parent’s tongue at Rank 2 and the other at Rank 1. Civilized tongues typically include human, elf, halfling, and dwarf; uncivilized tongues include wolfkin, orc, goblin,
ogre, and similar wild-blooded peoples. A “trade tongue” based on the human language remains common in market towns, but most non-human kin still prefer to converse privately in their own speech.

You can learn or increase ranks in locales with enough kin that speak the language by learning by practice, or be taught by a teacher. You do not have to make WITS rolls if the teacher is of the same kin as the language, even if they do not have the TEACHER talent.

• ✦ RANK 1: You speak the language crudely in its basic form. Everyone can tell this language is not native to you, and your accent may be jarring to some. You must make an INSIGHT or LORE roll to understand the meaning of complex spoken form such as diplomatic parlay, storytelling, or poetry.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You speak the spoken language fluently, with an accent of your locale. You have full grasp of the language in even complex conversations.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You speak the language with mastery over its many accents. You may pass as a local of a village you visited for at least a day, or as someone raised by that kin unless a Challenging LORE or INSIGHT roll is passed by more than one ⚔️.

segments.html: RAVALNDIC: Talked by the Ailanders, but it has become the most common secondary language among others. About 90% Alderlandic with a mix of Elven, Eori and Dwarven. So you may might understand some single words in overheard conversations, when the languages shares similarities. Dialects: Choose a region in the Ravenlands.
ALDERLANDIC: The mother tongue of the Alderlanders. The humans of the Ravenland see it

as a noble language and it is common that many books are written in Alderlandic. Both the rust brothers and the snake church see it as their official language which have helped to preserve its status in the Ravenlands. Dialects: Rust speech (mostly spoken in the western Ravenlands) and Old speech/Snake tongue (eastern Ravenlands).

ASLENI: The mother tongue of the Aslene. A fiery and expressive language. Those who speak Ravalndic can recognize many words, for example things like gold, nobility and titles, horrors, theatrical plays, and also some around nomadic life-style. Uses an alphabet that is similar to the old English one. Dialects: One for each of the Aslene clans. Quardic (from those that arrived and settled) and Galandic (the latter, more nomadic) are the common ones in the Ravenlands.

ELVEN: The language of the elves. It is soft and melodic that most listeners perceive as beautiful and singing. Those who speak Ravalndic can recognize many words that have to do with nature, magic and art. Uses soft rolling runs in writing. Dialects: There are no dialects among the elves in the Ravenlands, but it is instead hard to master. Increase the cost to learn it by +1 point, you may learn a “broken version” for 1 point, and that will make you understand each other.

DWARVEN: The language of the dwarves. Often perceived as mushy and cruel with long sentences. Those who speak Ravalndic can recognize many words that have to do with mountains, forging and mining. Uses angular runes in writing. Dialects: One per clan. In the Ravenlands choose between: Belderanic, Meromannic, Canidic or Crombic.
ORCISH: A language developed from a mix of Dwarf, Elven and later also Ravalndic. Orc males’ speech difficulties have had a strong impact on its
development. Has no written language of their own, but literate orcs use the general alphabet. Dialects: One per clan, in Ravenlands those would be Urhur, Roka and Visir. Plus one for the Viraga.

EORI: This language is spoken by halflings and goblins, though in two distinctly different dialects. Those who speak Ravalndic can recognize many words that have to do with cooking, beekeeping and brewery. Dialects: Goblin and Halfling.
WOLF TONGUE: The language of the wolfmen. No connection to other languages. Sounds most like animal sounds for the uninitiated. Can be howled over long distances. No written language.

SAURIAN: The language of the Saurian people. Have no connections to other languages. They only use the vowels a, u, and e, but have their own consonants of which eight are throat clicks that are reminiscent of “g”, and smacking sounds that are close to “t”. Their speech most closely resembles long, rambling harangues of syllables.

You have had dealings with rare cultures or creatures that have developed their own spoken language or similar means of communication. You may learn exotic Languages, for example: Ancient (still spoken by some Giants and Trolls), Deep Dwelver, Demonic, Dragon speech, Whiner; or other languages the GM mentions. These forgotten or forbidden languages do not belong to any common kin and cannot be learned with the LANGUAGE talent directly except through this talent. This talent can only be taught by teachers or members of rare cultures and never learned by practice.

• ✦ RANK 1: You gain a Rank 1 Language from the list above.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You gain a Rank 1 Language from the list above.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You increase one Language learned through this talent from Rank 1 to Rank 2, and gain another Rank 1 Language from the list above.
  • ✦ RANK 4: You increase one Language learned through this talent from Rank 1 to Rank 2, and gain another Rank 1 Language from the list above.
  • ✦ RANK 5: You increase one Language learned through this talent from Rank 2 to Rank 3, and another from Rank 1 to Rank 2. You can even fairly quickly decipher unknown and dead languages with a LORE roll.

segments.html: You have become studied and patient enough to pass your vast knowledge in digestible form to the eager and impressionable young minds who will inherit your wisdom for the next generation. Your services become more valuable, you normally can charge up to 20% more for your services per rank in this talent, should Students be able to afford such a price increase for the services you provide.
• ✦ RANK 1: Your student no longer needs to make a WITS roll when they spend a Quarter of a Day to learn a skill or talent from you.
itemLiHtmls: • ✦ RANK 1: Your student no longer needs to make a WITS roll when they spend a Quarter of a Day to learn a skill or talent from you.

segments.html:
• ✦ RANK 2: While you teach a Student a skill or talent, you may observe their use of another skill or talent that you may learn from them within the same Quarter of the Day. The Student must be willing to reveal and exchange their experience with you this way, and such exchange may allow some Students barter their knowledge instead of paying for tuition. The skill must use the same attribute, or the talent must be the same category (Class or General, but Kin Talents are not learned this way). All normal rules for learning apply for you as a Teacher, and you must make a WITS roll as normal without the benefit of RANK 1.
  • ✦ RANK 3: While taught by you, your Student can now learn faster than normal by making a WITS roll. If they get two ⚔️ or more, this teaching session counts as that many Quarters of the Day towards learning the skill or talent. Also, when you use RANK 2, you benefit from RANK 1 and no longer make WITS rolls.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When your Student makes a WITS roll using RANK 3, they may add number of bonus dice equal to your WITS attribute. You also benefit from RANK 3 when the Student exchanges a skill with you during the same Quarter of a Day.
  • ✦ RANK 5: When your Student makes a WITS roll using RANK 3, they can exchange one die for a D8 Artifact Die. You also benefit from RANK 4 when the Student exchanges a skill with you during the same Quarter of a Day.

segments.html: This is a talent that is typically found among NPCs in the Forbidden Lands and makes learning from them faster and more guaranteed than among players. However nothing stops players to invest in Rank 1 of the Talent to avoid having to make WITS rolls.
Your bodily grace amazes.

• ✦ RANK 1: You get a +1 bonus when you roll for MOVE to reduce FALL, BALANCE, RETREAT, or FLEE.
  • ✦ RANK 2: If you successfully negate an attack by DODGING and remain standing, you may simultaneously RETREAT one zone, ignoring nearby enemies.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can add a D8 Artifact Die when you roll for MOVE to FALL, BALANCE, RETREAT, or FLEE.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Halve any damage received from falling, being thrown or failing a FLEE action or retreat. Halve damage before applying reductions and round down.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Replace the D8 die from RANK 3 with a D12 die.

• ✦ RANK 3: You can add a D8 Artifact Die when you roll for MOVE to FALL, BALANCE, RETREAT, or FLEE.
• ✦ RANK 4: Halve any damage received from falling, being thrown or failing a FLEE action or retreat. Halve damage before applying reductions and round down.
• ✦ RANK 5: Replace the D8 die from RANK 3 with a D12 die.

segments.html: Through countless fight or flight situations, you've harnessed your adrenaline to act calculated rather give in to your emotions. This talent allows

you to gain special WP that are not added to your WP pool. You also can only have 1 special WP at the same time; extra are lost. Special WP must be spent until the end of your turn (your current turn if you gain it during your turn, or the end of your next turn if you gain it outside of your turn) or they are lost. You can also always burn that special WP to get 1 bonus die to an ATTACK or DODGE. Special WPs are lost at the end of a combat encounter.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you take 2 or more damage from an enemy attack during combat, you gain 1 special WP.
  • ✦ RANK 2: When you DODGE completely a monster attack during combat, you gain 1 special WP.
  • ✦ RANK 3: The first time you BREAK an enemy opponent in combat during each round, you gain 1 special WP.
  • ✦ RANK 4: You can also have up to 2 special WP at the same time. You now lose only one special WP at the end of a turn instead of all of them. When you burn special WP, you gain 2 bonus nice to ATTACK or DODGE instead of one.

segments.html: You can extract active substances from plants and animals to create potions with various effects. Doing so typically requires a cauldron, a heat source, HERBS, and a rare ingredient of some sort. Extracting such an ingredient from a monster requires a HEALING roll, and gives one dose per ⚔️ rolled. Example of potions can be found in the table below. You can find more examples under the Resources heading for monsters in the Bestiary.

STORAGE: Up to ten doses can be stored in a bottle or vessel that counts as a normal item. Five doses can be stored in a vessel that counts as a light item. The shelf life is very long, probably longer than the adventurers’short, hard lives.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can use the HEALING skill to concoct various types of potions. Each ⚔️ rolled gives you one dose.
  • ✦ RANK 2: As per rank 1, and you get +1 to all rolls for concocting potions.
  • ✦ RANK 3: As per rank 2, but you can add a D8 Artifact Die to all rolls for concocting potions.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Replace the D8 die with a D10 die.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Replace the D10 die with a D12 die.

segments.html: STANDARD OPTIONS

rows: Reduces the recovery time for critical injuries by half
Armor Rating +1 if applied to armor, the effect lasts a Quarter Day
The user's Wits is broken (no critical injury), but they may then ask a question to the GM who will answer cryptically but truthfully

segments.html: EXTENDED OPTIONS

Changed ingredients to not be as specifically tied to a certain monster and added more potions. You now always need at least a monster or group that together has 12+ Strength to have enough ingredients unless something else is mentioned. If you are missing just some Strength or have some in excess, your GM could allow you to roll with a -1 penalty per 2 points missing, or a +1 bonus per 3 points in excess.

segments.html: You are skilled in fighting with one close combat weapon in each hand. You have a primary weapon in your favored (or sword) hand and a secondary weapon in your other hand. You can draw both weapons with a single DRAW WEAPON action.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can use your secondary weapon to perform one extra attack per round as a fast action. It must be a LIGHT weapon, and the attack must be modified by -2.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Same as per RANK 1, but you can use a normal weapon as your secondary weapon.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Same as per RANK 2, and your attack with your secondary weapon is not modified.

segments.html: Animals respect you.

• ✦ RANK 1: Gain a +1 modifier when you try to calm or train an animal. You can train a tame animal to one of the following roles. This is done as when using animal handling to tame wild animals, although dogs will not roll for opposed strength. An animal can learn a maximum of one tricks category plus one for each skill level in ANIMAL HANDLING you have. See below for available categories to teach.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You make sure your food doubles as snacks for animals. If you have the time to give out food, you may add any successes ⚔️ from your food resource die to the CALM ANIMAL or TRAIN ANIMAL roll, adding any successes, but also risk reducing your available food.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can add a D8 Artifact Die when you try to calm or train an animal. An animal can now learn up to a maximum of two trick categories plus one for each skill level in animal handling you have.

  • ✦ RANK 5: Replace the D8 die with a D12 die. An animal can now learn up to three categories plus one for each skill level in ANIMAL HANDLING you have. segments.html: TRAINING CATEGORIES
You can choose from the following categories when TRAINING an animal or monster.

• ✦ Tricks: You have taught your animal some basic party tricks, like "Come," "Sit," "Play dead," "Roll over," "Bark," "Spin," "Drop it," and "Beg." The exact tricks it will know will vary depending on the animal. These tricks can be taught even without the Animal Whisperer talent.
  • ✦ Ride: You can mount/ride the animal, and it will listen to your commands. This training is included for non-predatory animals like horses when they are tamed. It cannot be applied to animals that cannot physically be ridden.
  • ✦ War: You no longer need to make an ANIMAL HANDLING roll to keep an animal from fleeing if it is wounded, there are loud noises, a heavy smell of blood, or there is general confusion around it. This training is only necessary for "prey animals" and is naturally learned behavior for predators.

segments.html:
• ✦ War II: Requires War. You have applied even more training for extreme situations so that it ignores fear attacks, being surrounded by fire, or hearing nearby powerful explosions.
  • ✦ Attack: You spend a FAST action to have your animal to engage in the same zone and attack a target once. If you have multiple trained animals, you must take SLOW action to direct up to two of them.
  • ✦ Guard: After giving the command, it will alert the owner (or wake them) to any presence of danger it perceives. It can also add a gear dice to a lookout's SCOUTING rolls.
  • ✦ Hunt: When hunting, you can replace the SURVIVAL roll to find your prey with an animal handling roll and add one gear die to represent the animal.
  • ✦ Hunt II: Requires Hunt. You can send out the animal to hunt independently. Roll your animal handling for the initial hunt roll, and add one gear dice to represent the animal. If you roll multiple ⚔️, reroll on the hunting table until an animal it can hunt is found. Any prey larger than your hunting animal will not be targeted; your hunting animal will then return empty-handed, but if it is smaller, it automatically succeeds. If the initial roll fails, the hunting mishap can result in your animal returning wounded.
  • ✦ Track: By letting your animal sniff at something that belongs to a target, it can track it by scent, following it up to a number of days equal to your animal handling roll.
  • ✦ Herd: Automatically succeeds any rolls to heard animals.

segments.html: Nothing splits a shield - or a skull - like a mighty axe.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you fight with an axe, your attack rolls are modified by +1.
  • ✦ RANK 2: When you hit an enemy with your axe and inflict at least one point of damage, you automatically inflict a critical injury (slash wound). The critical injury itself doesn't break your opponent - unless it kills them. No effect against monsters or animals.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can add a D8 Artifact Die to all attack rolls with an axe
  • ✦ RANK 4: When you deal a critical injury with an axe, treat your rank in EXECUTIONER as if it was two ranks higher.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you perform a SNEAK ATTACK, then if you use a LIGHT melee weapon, you may use SLEIGHT OF HAND instead of MELEE to perform it. If you use SLEIGHT OF HAND, the attack ignores your victim's armor.

segments.html:
• ✦ RANK 2: Your SLEIGHT OF HAND SNEAK ATTACK that inflicts at least one point of damage, makes your target unable to speak or run away during his upcoming round.
  • ✦ RANK 3: Your sleight of hand sneak attacks that inflict at least one point of damage also become an opposed roll vs the target's ENDURANCE. If the roll isn't successfully opposed (reduced to zero ⚔️), the target is automatically Broken and suffers a critical injury. Monsters are immune.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When attacking someone unaware of your presence or engaged in combat with a third party at ARM'S LENGTH, your attacks inflict an additional +1 damage.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Ranged weapons can now be used to make SLEIGHT OF HAND SNEAK ATTACK, as long as they are used at a maximum of SHORT range.

segments.html: When you are Broken, you can choose to unleash a primal rage upon the world. On your turn in the next round, you recover as many points in the attribute decreased to zero as your rank in BERSERKER. You must immediately attack the nearest opponent in close combat and keep fighting until you are Broken (again) or until all opponents within sight have been Broken. During your rage, you are immune to any attempts to MANIPULATE you and all your close combat attacks do one extra point of damage. If Broken during a BERSERKER rage, you cannot use this talent.
• ✦ RANK 5: You can restore one more point than possible in the attribute, temporarily raising its maximum. Any excessive points are lost when the rage ends.

segments.html: You have learned how to turn wood and leather into lethal bows and slings.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can use the CRAFTING skill to make ranged weapons from the weapons table, with average stats. You can make melee weapons out of bone.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You can make ranged weapons with a Weapon Bonus that is one point higher than usual. This takes twice as long, and your CRAFTING roll is modified by -2. You can make war bows and flint-knapped arrows and weapons. You get a +1 modification to CRAFTING and repair rolls for bowyer items.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can make ranged weapons with a Weapon Bonus that is two points higher than usual. This takes four times as long, and your CRAFTING roll is modified by -4. You can make composite bows, composite crossbows, and rawhide backings. Instead of the +1 modification, you may add a D8 Artifact Die to CRAFTING and repair rolls for bowyer items.
  • ✦ RANK 4: You can make ranged weapons with a Weapon Bonus that is three points higher than usual. This takes eight times as long, and your CRAFTING roll is modified by -6. You may craft two bowyer items simultaneously, provided you have the required materials. Replace the D8 with a D10 Artifact Die.
  • ✦ RANK 5: You can make ranged weapons with a Weapon Bonus that is four points higher than usual. This takes sixteen times as long, and your CRAFTING roll is modified by -8. Replace the D10 with a D12 Artifact Die.

You know how to cook using simple things, even while on a journey through the wilderness. Your CHEF talent also allows you to brew alcoholic beverages like beer, ale, mead, and wine. However, you cannot distill them into Liquor.
You can learn CHEF Rank 1 without a teacher by cooking to survive. This costs 3 XP but takes three Quarter Days of training. Make the normal WITS roll after each Quarter Day.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can turn up to D6 units of VEGETABLES, MEAT, or FISH into FOOD (see Chapter 7). Cooking requires a fire and takes a Quarter Day. You can cook up to a dozen units of FOOD in a proper kitchen in a Quarter Day.

segments.html:
• ✦ RANK 2: When you cook for a Quarter Day, you create an extra FOOD unit.
  • ✦ RANK 3: The food you cook is so delicious that whoever eats it immediately recovers a point of lost Empathy. Rank 3 now also applies to brewed alcoholic beverages, so they are considered a masterwork and restore Empathy.
  • ✦ RANK 4: You can now find the time to cook 1 unit of food while doing other things once per Quarter Day.
  • ✦ RANK 5: You can make a feast when you cook. People who participate count as resting (but not sleeping) while eating and drinking during the same Quarter Day as you cook, and while doing this, they all fully restore all attributes and may raise their Willpower Points to their Empathy. A feast uses 1 unit of produced FOOD per participant and 1 unit of WATER or other beverage.

You are completely callous and can kill defenseless enemies without so much as a second's hesitation.

• ✦ RANK 1: You can perform a COUP DE GRACE after combat without spending a Willpower Point.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You can kill helpless non-combatants without rolling Empathy, spending WP, or suffering Empathy damage.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You recover a point of lost Empathy whenever you perform a COUP DE GRACE or killing blow.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Your killing blows and COUP DE GRACE attacks double as FEAR attacks against enemies within short range. Roll PERFORMANCE or MANIPULATION; you may distribute any rolled ⚔️ as Wits damage amongst your targets. Animals and monsters are immune.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Each COUP DE GRACE or killing blow you perform grants you a Willpower Point.

segments.html: You have learned to use various maneuvers in your fighting style.

• ✦ RANK 1: Before rolling an attack, you may announce you want to push the enemy in your chosen direction. If the attack gets two or more ⚔️, you may spend 1 WP and decrease your result by one ⚔️ , but the attack must remain with at least one ⚔️. If you do, you push your enemy away from you by up to 2 meters in a desired direction. This causes the enemy to disengage with all creatures it is engaged in combat with. If the direction you push the enemy in a damaging location, such as a lit fireplace, they take up to one or more additional🩸up to the DM. If you push the enemy in a difficult terrain or against a difficult or uneven surface, they get up to -2 dice until the end of their next turn or must make a MOVE roll to remain standing, up to the DM. This does not work against monsters.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Before rolling an attack, you may announce that you want to prone the enemy to the ground. If the attack gets two or more ⚔️, you may spend 1 WP and decrease your result by one ⚔️ , but the attack must remain with at least one ⚔️. If you do, you force the enemy to drop Prone. As long as the enemy is engaged with you, it must roll MOVE to stand up from prone and suffers -1 die modifier to that roll. This does not work against monsters.

segments.html:
• ✦ RANK 3: Before rolling an attack, you may announce you want to overextend the enemy so they cannot attack you on the next turn. If the attack gets two or more ⚔️, you may spend 1 WP and decrease your result by one or two ⚔️ , but the attack must remain with at least one ⚔️. If you decrease by a single ⚔️, the enemy has -2 dice to their ATTACK or PARRY you until the end of their next turn, and cannot DISENGAGE or FLEE from you. If you decrease by two ⚔️, the enemy cannot ATTACK, PARRY, DISENGAGE or FLEE you until the end of their next turn. This does not work against monsters.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Before rolling an attack, you may announce you want to impale the enemy so the weapon goes through and lodges into them. If the attack gets three or more ⚔️, you may spend 1 WP and decrease your result by two ⚔️ , but the attack must remain with at least one ⚔️. If you do, your weapon impales and lodges into the enemy. Your attack does an additional 🩸 damage, or two 🩸 if it is two-handed stabbing weapon. Your weapon can no longer be used to make more attacks and remains impaled until you disengage with the impaled enemy or you attack another enemy with the same weapon. As long as it remains lodged into an enemy, that enemy can make an ENDURANCE roll to avoid taking 1 damage to STRENGTH at the start of their turn, and you have +2 dice to further attacks against the same enemy. As a fast or slow action, the enemy can attempt an ATTACK or DODGE roll to release themselves from your impalement. If they succeed, they are no longer impaled; if they fail, they take 1 damage to STRENGTH and remain impaled. In addition, RANK 1 and 2 now work against monsters.

segments.html: You are skilled at using weapons and shields to protect yourself in close combat.

• ✦ RANK 1: You get a +1 bonus to all PARRIES.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You get one free PARRY every round of combat. The extra PARRY does not count as one of your actions in the round.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can PARRY an unlimited number of times in the same round of combat, but only once against each attack. No matter how many times you PARRY, it will never count as more than one action.
  • ✦ RANK 4: When you don't PARRY an attack, you may add any held shield's Item Dice to your Armor Rating. You may now deflect projectiles with a weapon as a PARRY. Projectiles are treated as stab attacks (-2 penalty, or -4 without the parrying attribute).
  • ✦ RANK 5: When you don't PARRY an attack, you may add any held sheld's Item Dice to your DODGE roll. You can add a D8 Artifact Die to your roll when you PARRY.

segments.html: You know every trick in the book.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you use the FEINT action, you may throw dust in your opponents' eyes instead of swapping initiative segments as a SLEIGHT OF HAND roll. It counts as a piercing projectile attack for PARRY/DODGE and can only be parried with a shield. On a success, the target is blinded, as if in total darkness for 1 round per ⚔️. It cannot be used against monsters unless under very special circumstances (up to the GM).
  • ✦ RANK 2: When you use the FEINT action, you may, instead of swapping initiative segments, have the target lose all actions if you damage it with the next attack you take this round. The effect is reduced by 1 action per rank of the pain-resistant talent, and monsters are immune.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You may now use the FEINT action within NEAR range of your enemy. Also, when you use the FEINT action, you may, instead of swapping initiative segments, have the target be unable to DODGE or PARRY the next action you take this round.
  • ✦ RANK 4: You may use FEINT as a free action once per encounter (15 minutes).
  • ✦ RANK 5: As rank 4, but you may use each variant of FEINT as a free action once per encounter (15 minutes). You cannot use more than one of these free FEINT per round.

segments.html: You are an adept swimmer.

• ✦ RANK 1: While wearing no metal armor, you only need to roll for ENDURANCE every Quarter Day in water. You only need to roll for endurance to hold your breath every 10 rounds. Gain a +1 modifier to ENDURANCE rolls to stay afloat or hold your breath. You can SURVEY water hexes without a boat. Exchange the SCOUNTING roll for an ENDURANCE roll, including any bonuses from this talent. If done during spring/fall, you become COLD. It cannot be done during winter unless you have some magical immunity towards becoming COLD. The ability to hold your breath could ad-hoc give partial advantages near stinky enemies, etc.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You can swim as a FAST instead of a SLOW action, doubling your swim speed. Gain a D8 Artifact Die when you try to stay afloat, hold your breath, or SURVEY water hexes.
  • ✦ RANK 3: While submerged in water, you can now STAB, PARRY, DODGE, and PERFORM other actions the GM sees fit. These should normally be performed at a -2 penalty when submerged in water. Still, you are so adept at fighting underwater that you can turn the penalties into bonuses, i.e., gain a +2 bonus instead of a -2 penalty to actions like these.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Replace the D8 die with a D12 die.
  • ✦ RANK 5: You automatically succeed in any rolls to swim and can hold your breath for a turn (15 minutes) before you need to roll.

• ✦ RANK 1: All your attacks against monsters are modified by +1.

segments.html: You know where to strike to ensure your opponent falls and does not get up again. Ever.

• ✦ RANK 1: When you inflict a critical injury to your opponent, you can reverse the D66 roll for the critical injury - a roll of 16 becomes 61, for example.
  • ✦ RANK 2: Instead of RANK 1, you can reroll once. The highest roll counts.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can combine RANK 1 and RANK 2 effects. You can use them in any order you choose. You can forego the use of RANK 2 effect and change one die with a value of 5 to a value of 6.

  • ✦ RANK 5: If you reduce an enemy's Strength to zero, gain a Willpower Point. Monsters are no longer immune to critical injuries unless the GM sees fit (such as being incorporeal or not having defined anatomy).

segments.html: You can fire your bow or sling lightning fast. Hunters can combine this talent with PATH OF THE ARROW.

• ✦ RANK 1: You don't need to READY WEAPON before you SHOOT with a ranged weapon. Does not apply to crossbows.
  • ✦ RANK 2: You can SHOOT with a ranged weapon and RUN at the same time.
  • ✦ RANK 3: You only need to spend a fast action to SHOOT, meaning you can SHOOT twice in a round unless the weapon has LOAD. Whenever used, when your round ends, you take 1 Agility damage if you have moved zones more than once during this round.
  • ✦ RANK 4: Reloading a crossbow/firearm is now a FAST action. Shooting it still costs a SLOW action.
  • ✦ RANK 5: Once per round, if you spend a SLOW action to SHOOT, you gain a free action to SHOOT or RELOAD.

  • ✦ RANK 2: DISARMING you requires two extra ⚔️ - three ⚔️ for a one-handed weapon and four ⚔️ for a two-handed weapon.

  • ✦ RANK 5: You cannot be disarmed while holding a two-handed weapon in one hand.

segments.html: You are adept at running.

• ✦ RANK 1: You get a +1 modification when you roll MOVE to JUMP, RUN fast, FLEE, or because of rough terrain. If someone wants to RETREAT or FLEE from you, and nothing can hinder you from pursuing, add a -1 penalty to the enemy roll.
  • ✦ RANK 2: If you spend a slow action to run, you may traverse two zones. (In very open terrain, your superior movement could make you automatically win flee or opposed flee rolls.)
  • ✦ RANK 3: You can add a D8 Artifact Die when you roll for MOVE to UMP, RUN fast, FLEE, or because of rough terrain. If someone wants to RETREAT or FLEE from you, and nothing can hinder you from pursuing, add another -1 penalty to the enemy roll (to a total of -2).
  • ✦ RANK 4: Gain one free run action per turn, i.e., usable once every 15 minutes.
