rows: Orphaned. No family, no hearth. You cared for yourself since before you could choose to.
One village, shrine, or ferryman once showed you mercy.
Herder. You walked the herd roads early, sleeping close to livestock, dreaming of something wider.
One old herd-route or pasture still feels like yours.
Vagabond. Your family moved between villages, hiding from the Mist, never staying long enough to call a place home.
You carry one rumor about a ruined stead, bridge, or hidden shelter.
Squire. You carried steel and tended horses for someone stronger and learned your place before your name.
One former master, quartermaster, or stablehand still remembers your service.
Laborer. Grain, mud, and livestock filled your days. Something else filled your dreams.
You owe labor, coin, or gratitude to one farming family.
Hard Studies. A learned keeper set you to elder writings. The days were long, but truth repaid the work.
You possess one scrap of writing, copied prayer, or family secret.
Child of the Raven. You grew among the Raven Sisters and learned their signs before their reasons.
One old shrine, raven sign, or wandering sister still matters to you.
Druid's Apprentice. A druid took you young and showed you rites your village feared and needed in equal measure.
You remember a rite, warning, or path your teacher never finished explaining.
Guardian. Shield and sword came early. You wore your first scar before your first true name.
One kin elder trusts you to stand when others run.
Wanderer. Your kin moved constantly in the Mist years. You walked farther as a child than most adults ever will.
You know one safe sleeping place from the bad years of the Mist.
Laborer. Soil, stone, or timber filled your childhood for kin who needed hands more than promises.
You left kin behind who still expect your hands at harvest or lambing.
Herder. Flock roads and cattle fords gave you patience, calluses, and a life tied to the seasons.
One flock-road, cattle ford, or grazing debt binds you to a place.
Born in the Saddle. Your clan put you on horseback before your legs could grip the flanks.
One beast still knows your scent, or one clan elder does.
Dreamer. You lingered at fires, drinking in legends of Horn and the old wars while others slept.
You know one half-remembered legend others dismiss too quickly.
Strongest of the Clan. Bigger and fiercer than the rest even as a child. Others watched with envy or fear.
One childhood rival still measures themself against you.
Taught by a Wise Woman. A clan healer taught you signs, herbs, and the weight of the stories behind them.
You carry one charm, herb-lore habit, or whispered taboo.
Hunter. You tracked and killed before your adult teeth showed. The clan expected nothing less.
One kill, trail, or beast-sign from childhood still haunts your sleep.
Child of the Winds. A highland pilgrimage broke your childhood short. The road taught you what the clan could not.
You have slept in holy or cursed places and learned one omen there.
On the Run. Your family kept moving. Someone wanted you found, or simply gone.
Someone once hunted you or your family and may still want the work finished.
Artist. Your hands found form, color, or sound before your voice found argument.
You are remembered by one patron, troupe, or jealous rival.
Student. Books and fragments drew you more than play. A sage bent your curiosity toward the deeper writings.
You carry one copied diagram, poem, sign, or occult note.
Acrobat. You climbed everything: roofs, beams, bridges, trees. Height was home.
You know roofs, beams, and narrow places in one settlement better than its watch does.
Fighter. You learned steel early. Bruises and drill became your language.
One old drill-master or war veteran still knows your name.
Ghost Child. You belonged to no one. A loose pack of strays and cast-offs took you in.
You belong to a loose pack of strays, thieves, or cast-offs.
Baker's Apprentice. Flour, fire, and the smell of dough. Comfort was all you knew until it wasn't.
One oven-house, cookfire, or feast-hall would still take you in.
Laborer. Small hands, long hours. Grain, cattle, and the ache of honest work.
You left behind a field, a beast, or a family argument over work.
Craftsman. Clever fingers from the start, and a hunger to see the work of better hands than yours.
You own or crave one fine tool made by better hands than yours.
Raised in the Kitchen. Gossip, grease, and sharp blades taught you how a household runs behind its manners.
You learned how gossip moves through a house faster than smoke.
Bookworm. While others played, you read. Tales and fragments became more real than neighbors.
One book, fragment, or old tale has grown too important in your mind.
Loner. You smiled at kin and kept your own counsel. Nobody noticed until you were already gone.
You know how to smile at kin while keeping your own counsel.
Smith's Apprentice. Heat, iron, and the rhythm of the hammer. You still owe loyalty to a forge or a master.
You still owe a master, forge, or god-marked tool your loyalty.
Mineborn. Darkness, cold stone, and the slow drip of hidden water made you what you are.
You know one shaft, seam, or buried way not found on any proper map.
Scout's Apprentice. Sharp eyes earned you a place on the watch. You learned to see danger before it moved.
One watch-post, cairn, or hidden cut in the hills remains in your memory.
Guardian-in-Training. Steel, oath, and duty came before play. A proud warrior shaped you in their image.
One oath of defense still weighs on you, fulfilled or not.
Carver. You learned where stone yields and where it refuses. That knowledge earned respect and cost you time.
You know how stone yields, and where it refuses. That knowledge has a price.
Hard Studies. A learned elder set you to old writings. The work was long, but knowledge repaid the effort.
You carry one fragment of elder writing or one argument you still mean to prove.
Loner. You stood at the edge of your own people for years and learned to prefer it there.
You spent years at the edge of your own people and learned to stay there.
Fighter. An elder warrior tested you against the memory of an old war no one has forgotten.
One elder warrior still measures you against an old war no one has forgotten.
Child of the Forest. One grove, spring, or ancient tree still answers to your memory across the centuries.
One tree, spring, or grove still answers to your memory.
Hard Studies. You remember words, names, or signs others wish had stayed buried.
You remember words, names, or signs others wish buried.
Wanderer. The road taught you what your own halls would not admit.
The road taught you what your own halls would not.
Druid's Apprentice. Your teacher is dead, gone, or listening from somewhere you cannot reach.
A teacher is dead, gone, or listening from somewhere you cannot reach.
Wolfling. The pack raised you before the clan did. You still think like a wolf when startled.
You still think of one wolf pack, or one pack thinks of you.
Scrounger. You learned early that possession is a thought, not a fence.
You know where things vanish in one camp, ruin, or market.
Child of the Woods. Trees, roots, and undergrowth were your first walls. The forest was safer than any house.
One grove, path, or den still feels guarded by kin you cannot name.
Wildling. Your clan taught freedom first and obedience never. That still costs you.
Your freedom is a bruise that never heals and a debt that never clears.
Wanderer. You knew more roads as a child than most adults learn in a lifetime.
You know one shelter from old Mist nights that others would miss in daylight.
Storyteller. An elder's tales gripped you by the fire and would not let go. Now the stories are yours to carry.
One clan elder's tale still points toward treasure, shame, or revenge.
Minstrel. You learned blood-songs and betrayal-chants young. They still start fights if you sing them aloud.
One blood-song you know can still start a fight if sung in the wrong hall.
Worker. Your hands remember labor done for others, and the anger has not left them.
The anger from years of working for others has not left your hands.
Brigand. You wronged someone on a hungry road, or they wronged you. It started early and never ended clean.
You wronged someone, or they wronged you, on a road neither of you chose.
Drifter. No camp held you long. Restless legs and thin patience kept you moving.
One road band, camp, or hidden ford still lies under your memory.
Warrior. Blood bought you respect before words ever could. You learned that before your growth was done.
You know what respect looks like when it is bought in blood.
Loner. You saw more than your people wanted you to see. Keeping it to yourself became a habit.
You have one reason not to trust your own people first.
Howler. You ran with howlers between the clans, learning the old laments by heart and by scent.
You know one old clan lament and the name bound to it.
Hunter. The pack taught you blood, spoor, and patience before you had a name for them.
One beast-sign, hunting ground, or old kill-site still draws you back.
Outcast. Your own pack turned its back. The forest became your kin instead.
You still smell the moment your pack turned its back on you.
Tracker. Your nose ran faster than your feet. You found things others walked past without a thought.
You can still find one person, beast, or camp by habit if not by scent.
Fighter. Strongest in the litter. Dominance came fast and cost more than you knew.
You learned early what dominance costs and what it does not win.
Child of the Forest. Bark, root, herb, and still water shaped you before any elder's hand did.
One herb-wife, lake, or hollow tree still feels like kin ground.

segments.html: Choose Young, Adult, or Old as described in Chapter 2. Your age determines three things: how many attribute points you spend, how many general talents you choose, and how many life cycles you resolve.

A cycle is one chapter of your character's past — a stretch of years spent in a single way of life. A cycle as a Fighter means years under arms. A cycle as a Peddler means years on the trade roads. Each cycle contains four turns, and each
turn is one beat of that life: an arrival, a hardship, a rise, or a reckoning. You make one turn test per turn, so each turn produces exactly one skill mark.

The "Cycles" column is the total number of life cycles, including the first. Your first cycle is always shortened — childhood covers its first two turns, so you resolve only its third and fourth. The "Turns You Resolve" column counts only the turns where you roll dice. Each turn produces one skill mark, and the two marks from your childhood foundation bring the total to 8, 12, or 16 — matching the standard method's skill point budget exactly.
Elves cannot begin as Young. They begin at Adult or Old.

The first cycle is shorter. You resolve only the Third Turn and the Fourth Turn of your first cycle, not all four. Your childhood foundation covers the early years — the two skill marks it granted already account for the First Turn and the Second Turn. You step into the story at the moment life starts demanding something of you. Every cycle after the first runs the full four turns.

A cycle covers a different span of calendar time depending on kin. The four turns within a cycle divide that span roughly but not equally — a turn is not a fixed number of months. It is one reach of the story: brief if the wheel bites fast, long if the years grind.

For each completed cycle, choose or roll a life path from the list later in this section. Then resolve the turns of that cycle in order — two turns in the first cycle (starting from the third one), four in every cycle after that. At the end of each cycle, roll for advancement or departure before moving to the next cycle.
Every cycle has four turns, each carrying a different weight.

rows: Learning, first patron, first duty, rough initiation
Hunger, fear, obligation, debt, quarrel, hard weather
Promotion, discovery, recognition, temptation, secret knowledge
Betrayal, battle, scandal, oath, escape, inheritance, ruin

segments.html: Each path in this section has a separate event table for every turn, so the story shifts as the cycle progresses. If a turn gives you a choice between two skills, the player decides which one fits the story better.
For each turn, follow these steps.

Step 1: Make the Turn Test. Every life path has a turn test — one or two skills that say whether the character stayed afloat in that kind of life. Roll against your current rank in the chosen skill. If the skill is still 0, roll the linked attribute only.
Step 2: Apply the Result.

rows: Mark 1 skill from the path's hard-lesson list. Then roll on the path's mishap table.
Mark 1 skill from the path's normal skill list. Then roll on the turn's event table.
As success, and gain either 1 edge on the event roll or 1 extra silver die if the event grants money.

segments.html: Step 3: Mark Wear. If a failed turn test follows another failed turn test within the same cycle, add 1 Wear mark. A single failure followed by a success does not add Wear — only sustained hardship leaves a lasting mark. At the end of character creation, total your Wear:

• 0–1 Wear: no extra effect.
  • 2–3 Wear: choose one scar, rival, debt, or lingering fear.
  • 4+ Wear: choose one of those, then also begin play with either a chronic pain, a feud, or lowered Standing in one settlement.
itemLiHtmls: • 0–1 Wear: no extra effect.
• 2–3 Wear: choose one scar, rival, debt, or lingering fear.
• 4+ Wear: choose one of those, then also begin play with either a chronic pain, a feud, or lowered Standing in one settlement.

segments.html: Wear creates fiction, not hidden numerical punishment. Young characters often walk away clean. Old characters, who resolve more turns and face narrowing penalties on repeated paths, carry the heaviest weight.

Each time the life generator tells you to gain a skill, you do not raise the rank directly. Instead, you mark one tally beside that skill. The tally tracks how often life pushed you in that direction. Final rank depends on how many marks you accumulate:
Marks between thresholds are not wasted — they count toward the next rank. A skill with 4 marks is Rank 3, one mark short of Rank 4.

Unspent marks at the end of generation. After all marks have been converted to ranks, count any marks that did not reach the next threshold — the 4th mark in a skill at Rank 3, the 6th mark in a skill at Rank 4, the leftover tally that fell short. Each such mark converts to 3 XP at the start of play. This covers skills and talent marks alike.

The same progression applies to talent ranks gained through advancement benefits. If a path's advancement table grants Rank 1 in a talent, mark one tally for that talent. A second grant of the same talent adds a second mark. Two marks raise the talent to Rank 2.

Early lessons come fast; later mastery comes slow. A character who spent most of a lifetime in one calling may reach Rank 3 or Rank 4 in its central skill. Rank 4 is the territory of Old characters whose every cycle bent the same direction. Rank 5 requires seven marks in a single skill, which means almost nothing else developed. If marks would push a skill to Rank 4 or higher, check with the GM before locking it in. Some tables set Rank 3 as the ceiling for starting characters and open the higher ranks only when the character's history makes a compelling case.

Some events and mishaps carry an italic tag: This may be your Pride or This may be your Dark Secret. These are not requirements. They are offers the life generator makes when an event carries the right weight — a triumph worth remembering, or a stain worth hiding.

If a character encounters one of these during generation, the player may claim it as a note about where their Pride or Dark Secret comes from. Only one Dark Secret may be claimed this way. Pride itself is not chosen here; every adventurer has it. If no Dark Secret was claimed during the life generator, choose from the profession entry as normal.

Not every event carries a tag. The ones that do are the kind of moments that mark a life — the kill that made your name, the order you should not have obeyed, the rite you will not speak of, the season you survived when no one else did.
Most paths have no threshold. If the story allows it, a character may enter.
Some paths assume training, access, or recognized standing before a character may walk them:

rows: Fighter, Rogue, Hunter, Drifter, Laborer, Outcast, Captive
One completed Fighter or Champion cycle and a named oath, cause, charge, or sworn patron
Lore 1 or Healing 1, or a shrine, grove, teacher, or sacred duty in the story
Lore 1, or an occult contact, teacher, grimoire fragment, or marked sign in the story
Performance 1 or Manipulation 1, or a patron, troupe, or hall that would take you in
Manipulation 1 or Insight 1, or trade goods, caravan work, or a market contact in the story
Animal Handling 1 or Move 1, or access to a herd, mount, or riding household in the story

segments.html: If a character does not meet a path's threshold, choose another path for that cycle. If no other path makes sense, the character falls into one of the crisis paths — Drifter, Laborer, Outcast, or Captive — whichever best fits the event that broke the old life.

The Champion's Calling. Champion is not an ordinary childhood path. A rare few are chosen before their martial life has truly begun. If you enter the Fighter path for your first cycle, roll a D6 before resolving its Third Turn — your first resolved turn in that path. On a 5–6, a temple, household, war leader, surviving oathbound, or other cause recognizes something in you and offers a charge. You may accept and replace Fighter with Champion for that cycle, waiving the normal requirement to have completed a Fighter cycle. Name the oath, cause, charge, or sworn

patron with the GM before resolving the turn. On a 1–4, or if you refuse the offer, continue in Fighter as normal. The GM may instead create a formative event that offers access to the Champion path. If it occurs before your first resolved Fighter turn and you accept its charge, replace Fighter with Champion for the current cycle. If it occurs later in a Fighter cycle, accepting it qualifies you to enter Champion in your next cycle. Refusing the charge leaves you a Fighter. The calling grants no extra skill mark or benefit beyond those stated by the formative event.

Childhood. If your childhood foundation lists a Suggested Path and that path has a threshold, the childhood waives it. You enter that path for your first cycle without meeting the skill or story requirement. Growing up inside a way of life counts as the threshold — the household, the trade, the mark on the land. This exception applies only to the first cycle. Thresholds apply normally when entering the same path again in a later cycle, because by then you are choosing it rather than being shaped by it.

Using story context instead of a skill threshold? Check with the GM first. The story-based substitutes above assume that teachers, patrons, and institutions are available somewhere in the world your group is building. Some campaigns begin in places where they are not — a remote frontier, a world of collapsed order, a starting scenario of pure hardship where no guild masters, grove keepers, or learned merchants are

within reach. In those settings the GM may rule that the story threshold cannot be claimed for a given path. This is not a punishment; it is the world telling the character that the road to that life is not open here yet. A Sorcerer does not emerge from a village that has never seen a grimoire. A Druid does not come from country that burned its last grove. Those paths become available once the campaign makes room for them.
At the end of each cycle, roll once on the path's advancement table using one of the path's turn test skills.

rows: You leave that path. Roll or choose a new one next cycle.
You may remain in the same path next cycle. Roll once on the advancement benefits table and take the result.
As success, but roll twice on the advancement benefits table. Each roll must produce a unique result — reroll duplicates. Take both.
As two successes, then choose one result from the remaining four options on the advancement benefits table. Take all three results.

segments.html: A character may remain in the same path across multiple cycles. A mercenary might stay a mercenary. A rider might never leave the saddle. But repetition narrows the life.
After the first completed cycle in the same path:

• Turn tests in the next same-path cycle are made at -1.
  • Failed turn tests roll mishaps with +1.
  • The same direct talent benefit cannot be gained twice from that path's advancement table.
itemLiHtmls: • Turn tests in the next same-path cycle are made at -1.
• Failed turn tests roll mishaps with +1.
• The same direct talent benefit cannot be gained twice from that path's advancement table.

segments.html: At the end of any cycle, a character may leave a path voluntarily — even after a successful advancement roll. No roll is needed. The old life has already paid for the next one.
The new path must follow the story. You do not move from a jail pit to horse-warrior without some road between them.
A cycle forces a path change when:

• A Fourth Turn event says you must change path.
  • A mishap says the path is broken.
  • You fail the advancement roll.
  • The story clearly destroys the old life.
itemLiHtmls: • A Fourth Turn event says you must change path.
• A mishap says the path is broken.
• You fail the advancement roll.
• The story clearly destroys the old life.

segments.html: When this happens, choose the next path from the event that caused the break. If the event does not name a path, roll on the forced-life table below.
Forced-Life Table

rows: Prison, stockade, hostage-taking, or war captivity
Debt, bond-service, confiscated goods, or a ruined bargain
Exile, outlawry, blood-feud, or banishment from kin
Patron slain, hall burned, company broken, or route collapsed
Crop failure, plague, winter hunger, or herd-loss
Scandal, sorcerous stain, shrine curse, or broken oath

segments.html: Choose the path that best fits the break. If more than one fits, the player chooses.

Prison, slavery, hostage-taking, and bond-service now have their own crisis path: Captive. Use it whenever the story puts a character in chains, behind bars, or under another person's control against their will. After the captivity ends, the character may return to a profession path if they meet its threshold — or fall into another crisis path if the damage was too deep.

Each profession path below represents a trade, calling, or way of life an adventurer followed between childhood and the day they took to the road. Every path has a turn test, a normal skill list, a hard-lesson skill list, four turn event tables, a mishap table, an advancement table, and a mustering-out table.
Profession paths lead toward one of the chapter's nine professions: Champion, Druid, Fighter,

Hunter, Minstrel, Peddler, Rider, Rogue, and Sorcerer. A character who completes a cycle in a profession path has taken a real step toward that calling — learning the skills, building the contacts, and earning the scars that shape a working life.
You put a promise above comfort, coin, and sometimes mercy. The cause gave your sword direction; the oath made turning back a kind of death.
Turn Test: Melee or Endurance. Normal Skills: Melee, Might, Endurance, Move, Survival, Insight. Hard-Lesson Skills: Endurance, Insight, Melee.

segments.text: Champion First Turn: Cause, Oath, and First Charge

rows: Words Before Witnesses. You swore yourself to a cause before folk who will remember. Gain Insight or Melee. Gain one sworn contact.
Weapon Vigil. Drill, prayer, and bruises taught your hands what conviction could not. Gain Melee or Might.
Shield Duty. You stood between danger and someone who could not face it alone. Gain Endurance or Melee.
Road of Devotion. Your cause sent you across bad country with little comfort. Gain Move or Survival.
Keeper of the Code. A priest, elder, veteran, or exile taught you the demands behind the words. Gain Lore or Insight.
First Charge. You were trusted with a person, relic, boundary, or message that could not be lost. Gain Survival or Scouting.

segments.text: Champion Second Turn: The Cost of Duty

rows: Public Provocation. Someone mocked your cause to test whether your oath ruled you or your temper did. Gain Insight or Melee. Gain one rival.
Hard Escort. You brought your charge through hunger, pursuit, or foul weather. Gain Move or Survival.
Unworthy Order. A patron demanded obedience where your conscience demanded refusal. Gain Manipulation or Insight. This may be your Dark Secret.
Lean Vigil. You kept watch while others slept and went without while others ate. Gain Endurance or Survival.
The Accused. Duty and justice pointed in different directions. Gain Insight or Manipulation.
Price of Loyalty. Coin, safety, or affection was offered for one small betrayal. Gain Might or Insight.

segments.text: Champion Third Turn: Deed and Doubt

rows: Held the Gate. You stood where others broke and bought their lives with blood. Gain Melee or Might. This may be your Pride.
Rescue Under Fire. You crossed danger to bring someone back. Gain Move or Endurance.
Nemesis Named. An enemy made your cause personal and promised to finish the quarrel. Gain Melee or Insight. Gain one rival.
Sign of the Cause. A relic, omen, bloodline, or old account gave your oath deeper roots. Gain Lore or Survival. Gain one rumor.
Promise Failed. You arrived too late, chose wrongly, or lacked the strength to keep your word. Gain Healing or Insight. Add one Wear. This may be your Dark Secret.
Rallied the Fearful. Others found courage because you refused to yield. Gain Manipulation or Endurance. Gain one grateful contact.

segments.text: Champion Fourth Turn: Fulfillment, Breaking, or Renewal

rows: Cause Destroyed. Your patron fell, shrine burned, bloodline ended, or order broke apart. Gain Survival or Insight. You must change path next cycle unless you give the cause a new form.
Oath Fulfilled. Against cost and doubt, you kept the promise that made you. Gain Melee or Insight. Gain +1 Standing among those who know the deed.
Costly Mercy. You spared someone your cause named as an enemy and accepted the consequences. Gain Healing or Endurance. Gain one contact or one rival.
Deed Proclaimed. Witnesses carried the story of your stand farther than you did. Gain Melee or Manipulation. This may be your Pride.
Named Oathbreaker. Whether the charge was true or false, people believed it. Gain Insight or Move. Gain one enemy and lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
Vow Renewed. Trial stripped your promise down to what you truly meant. Gain Endurance or Lore. You may take one Champion advancement benefit even if your later advancement roll fails.
You broke your word when keeping it mattered most. Gain one dark secret and one witness who remembers. This may be your Dark Secret.
Someone under your protection died. Gain one grieving contact or one enemy who holds you responsible.
Zeal made you cruel, blind, or easy to use. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
A rival defeated and marked you. Gain one scar and one nemesis.
Your patron betrayed the cause while demanding your loyalty. Turn one former contact into an enemy or begin play owing a dangerous service.
The cause demanded something you could not do. Your next cycle must change path unless you take one Wear and remain to confront it.
Your failure shattered the oath in public and brought ruin to those who trusted it. Gain one scar, one enemy, and lower Standing by 1 in two settlements. Your next cycle must change path.
One sworn ally, patron, shrine-keeper, or household contact
One-handed weapon, studded leather armor, and shield
One rumor about a lost relic, hidden heir, oathbound enemy, or abandoned cause
One good one-handed weapon and a serviceable shield
Studded leather armor and a closed helmet
One sworn contact and one enemy of the cause
2D6 copper and one duty that cannot be settled with coin
An oath-token, seal, relic fragment, or badge that opens one door and closes another
One rumor about a lost charge, hidden sanctuary, nemesis, or unfinished vow

segments.html: You learned the names the trees remember and the prices the land collects. Holy or cursed, it hardly matters — the work is the same.
Turn Test: Lore or Survival. Normal Skills: Lore, Survival, Healing, Insight, Animal Handling, Scouting. Hard-Lesson Skills: Healing, Insight, Lore.

segments.text: Druid First Turn: Shrine, Grove, or Wandering Teacher

rows: Shrine Duty. You kept a lonely holy place through rain and neglect. Gain Lore or Survival.
Herb Basket. You learned what heals, what numbs, and what kills. Gain Healing or Crafting.
Forest Warning. Something in the trees taught you caution. Gain Scouting or Animal Handling.
Pilgrim's Question. A stranger asked for truth and left trouble behind. Gain Insight or Manipulation.
Burial Work. You laid out dead kin, beast, or wanderer. Gain Healing or Lore.
Old Teacher. Someone showed you signs no village priest or Raven Sister would dare name. Gain Lore or Insight. Gain one druidic contact.

segments.text: Druid Second Turn: Weather, Duty, and Omen

rows: Flood or Drought. The land failed and folk came begging. Gain Survival or Healing.
Broken Beast. You saved or slew something wounded and dangerous. Gain Animal Handling or Marksmanship.
Sacred Boundary. You guarded a place others should not have crossed. Gain Melee or Scouting.
Bad Dream. Sleep brought warning, if not clarity. Gain Insight or Lore.
Village Suspicion. Someone called you holy, someone else called you cursed. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Long Forage. You lived lean and kept moving. Gain Survival or Scouting.

segments.text: Druid Third Turn: Power and Burden

rows: Hidden Pool. You found a place where the world felt thin. Gain Lore or Healing.
Protected the Wild. Men with axes or torches learned you would not step aside. Gain Marksmanship or Melee.
Spoken For. A chieftain, village, or clan sought your blessing. Gain Manipulation or Insight. This may be your Pride.
Spirit Sign. A beast, storm, or blight took on meaning for you. Gain Lore or Animal Handling.
Forbidden Rite. You stood too close to power and did not forget it. Gain Healing or Insight. Add one Wear. This may be your Dark Secret.
Gathered Favors. Quiet folk started owing you thanks. Gain Insight or Survival. Gain one contact.

segments.text: Druid Fourth Turn: Exile, Reverence, or Loss

rows: Driven Out. Someone feared your work or needed a scapegoat. Gain Survival or Move. You must change path next cycle unless protected by a strong contact.
Sacred Charge. You were entrusted with a place, relic, or oath. Gain Lore or Manipulation.
Plague Work. You stayed where others fled. Gain Healing or Endurance. Gain one scar or one grateful settlement. This may be your Pride.
Blighted Grove. Something ancient was spoiled, cut down, or burned. Gain Scouting or Insight. Gain one enemy tied to the deed.
Pilgrimage. You walked farther than you intended and learned the land by foot and hunger. Gain Survival or Lore.
Recognized as Wise. Word of your judgment spread. Gain Insight or Manipulation. You may take one Druid advancement benefit even if your later advancement roll fails.
You misread a sign and someone paid for it. Gain one guilty memory and one rival. This may be your Dark Secret.
A rite turned on you. Gain one scar or visible mark tied to the mishap.
Villagers denounced you. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
You protected the wrong thing, or at the wrong cost. Gain one enemy.
Something followed you out of a holy or cursed place. Gain one recurring omen.
Your teacher died, vanished, or condemned you. Your next cycle must change path unless you take one Wear.
A curse or spirit you mishandled turned outward before you could contain it. Gain one scar and one enemy, and lower Standing by 1 in one settlement. Your next cycle must change path.
Rank 1 in Path of Healing or Path of Sight
One shrine, circle, or wise contact
Staff, herbs, and a healer's satchel
One sacred rumor, hidden grove, or old curse the GM may develop later
Staff, herbs, and simple ritual tools
One wise contact and one suspicious priest, elder, or hunter
A sacred charm, rune-stick, or bark-scroll
D6 silver and one debt of gratitude from common folk
One scar from plague, rite, beast, or weather
One rumor about a hidden grove, blighted shrine, or ancient site

segments.html: You held a line, carried a blade, marched where you were told, and survived what should have killed you. The company, the levy, the hall-lord's retinue — the name of the service changes, but the steel does not.
Turn Test: Melee or Might
Normal Skills: Melee, Might, Endurance, Marksmanship, Move, Survival
Hard-Lesson Skills: Endurance, Melee, Might

segments.text: Fighter First Turn: Levy, Guard, or Blade for Hire

rows: Barracks Lesson. A hard sergeant beat fear out of you with a stave. Gain Melee or Endurance. You also gain a rival in the same company.
Shield Wall. You held a line for the first time and learned to trust wood and iron. Gain Might or Melee. If you already have a shield, it is scarred but serviceable.
Night Watch. You learned boredom, cold, and how danger sounds before it shows itself. Gain Scouting or Insight.
Hall-Lord's Favor. Someone above your station noticed you. Gain Manipulation or Melee. You also gain one contact tied to a hall, tower, or garrison.
Camp Sickness. Fever took half the tent rows. Gain Healing or Endurance. You also gain one Wear.
Spoils. The dead had no use for what they carried. Gain Survival or Melee. Roll one silver die and keep the result.

segments.text: Fighter Second Turn: March, Hunger, and Orders

rows: Long March. Your boots rotted and your back bent under the pack. Gain Survival or Endurance.
Dirty Work. You were ordered to do something shameful. Gain Insight or Manipulation. You also gain one rival or one dark memory. This may be your Dark Secret.
Rough Company. You learned how soldiers settle quarrels where no law can hear them. Gain Melee or Might.
Supply Raid. Hunger drove your band to theft, or your captain called it requisition. Gain Scouting or Move.
Winter Camp. Mud, wet wool, and thin stew taught you patience. Gain Endurance or Healing.
Veteran's Tale. An older fighter taught you where lines break and men lie. Gain Lore or Melee. You also gain one rumor about a battlefield, ruin, or buried standard.

segments.text: Fighter Third Turn: Battle and Promotion

rows: First Blood. You killed at arm's length and learned the sound it makes. Gain Melee or Marksmanship. This may be your Pride.
Standard Duty. You carried colors, messages, or commands through danger. Gain Move or Manipulation.
Arrow Storm. You survived what should have dropped you. Gain Endurance or Healing. You also gain one scar.
Picked for the Front. A captain trusted you where the line would buckle first. Gain Might or Melee.
Siege Work. You learned ladders, ropes, and patience under stones. Gain Crafting or Marksmanship.
Field Name. The company began calling you by deed instead of birth. Gain Melee or Insight. You also gain +1 Standing in one settlement tied to the campaign.

segments.text: Fighter Fourth Turn: Last Stand, Oath, or Defeat

rows: Broken Company. The banner fell, the captain died, or the pay chest vanished. Gain Survival or Scouting. You must change path next cycle unless you spend your advancement result to remain.
Honors Paid in Silver. Your service ended cleanly. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Roll two silver dice and keep the highest.
Bad Wound. You left the field alive but not whole. Gain Healing or Endurance. You also gain one Wear and one scar.

Sworn Blade. A hall-lord, clan chief, or war-band leader offered continued service. Gain Melee or Manipulation. You may remain in Fighter next cycle without an advancement roll if you accept that patron as a contact.
Massacre. You escaped what others did not. Gain Survival or Move. You also gain one rumor about the killer responsible.
Named in Victory. Your deed was seen and remembered. Gain Melee or Marksmanship. You may take one Fighter advancement benefit even if your advancement roll later fails. This may be your Pride.
Captured and stripped. Change your next cycle to Captive, Outcast, or Rogue.
Left for dead. Gain one scar and one enemy who thinks you should have stayed buried.
You obeyed a foul order. Begin play with a dark secret tied to that deed.
You deserted. Lower your Standing by 1 in one settlement that knows your face.
A comrade died because of you, or because you think so. Gain a grieving contact or a blood-feud rival.
Your body held, your nerve did not. Gain Insight or Endurance, then take one fear tied to fire, cavalry, sorcery, or enclosed places.
You survived a rout or siege that killed everyone you served with, and you came back changed. Gain two scars and one fear tied to fire, the dark, or enclosed ground. Your next cycle must change path.
One armor or weapon package of standard quality
One local reputation gain and one rumor about a ruin, battlefield, or old treasury
Chainmail or studded leather, worn but sound
One good weapon and one scar with a name behind it
One old comrade contact and one rumor about buried spoils
2D6 silver and one debt still unpaid
One mount or pack beast, not a warhorse
A banner scrap, officer's token, or campaign relic that can open one door and close another

segments.html: You fed the living by killing the wild. The forest taught patience, the quarry taught humility, and the cold taught you everything else.
Turn Test: Scouting or Marksmanship. Normal Skills: Scouting, Marksmanship, Survival, Animal Handling, Move, Crafting. Hard-Lesson Skills: Scouting, Survival, Marksmanship.

segments.text: Hunter First Turn: Trail, Bow, and Cold Camp

rows: Tracked Fresh Kill. You followed blood before you knew wisdom. Gain Scouting or Survival.
Learned the Bow. Someone corrected your hands until the shot flew true. Gain Marksmanship or Move.
Camp Meat. Others ate because you did not miss. Gain Survival or Animal Handling.
Snare Line. You learned patience from cord, branch, and spoor. Gain Crafting or Scouting.
Bad Weather. The sky taught you what pride is worth. Gain Endurance or Survival.
Old Forester. Someone taught you where beasts break and where men do. Gain Insight or Marksmanship.

segments.text: Hunter Second Turn: Range and Risk

rows: Wounded Beast. The prey doubled back and made you earn the kill. Gain Melee or Scouting.
Lean Season. You hunted for hungry folk and felt each empty day. Gain Survival or Insight.
Taken Trail. You found signs of other hunters where none should have been. Gain Scouting or Move. Gain one rival or rumor.
Long Shot. One arrow made your name in camp. Gain Marksmanship or Insight.
Beast Tamer. A dog, hawk, or stubborn mount taught you humility. Gain Animal Handling or Endurance.
Night Fire. Stories by the coals taught you the old paths of the land. Gain Lore or Survival.

segments.text: Hunter Third Turn: Reputation, Blood, and Teeth

rows: Big Kill. You brought down something folk feared. Gain Marksmanship or Melee. This may be your Pride.
Guide Work. You led others who knew less than they admitted. Gain Scouting or Manipulation.
Winter Hunger. You learned what men become when game runs thin. Gain Insight or Survival.
Territory Mark. You began to think of a stretch of land as yours. Gain Scouting or Animal Handling.
Rust or Raven. Rust Brothers, Raven Sisters, or tax-hands took interest in the woods. Gain Move or Insight.
Best Skin. A pelt, antler rack, or set of fangs bought you more notice than comfort. Gain Crafting or Marksmanship. Roll one silver die.

segments.text: Hunter Fourth Turn: Mastery or Mauling

rows: Mauled. You lived, but the beast left something behind in flesh or nerve. Gain Endurance or Healing. Gain one scar.
Named Guide. Caravans, scouts, or hall-lords sought your eye. Gain Manipulation or Scouting.
Poacher's Fight. Another hunter crossed your line or you crossed theirs. Gain Melee or Marksmanship. Gain one rival.
Forest Fire. Flame or smoke ruined land you knew by heart. Gain Survival or Move. You must change path next cycle unless revenge or duty keeps you here.
Trained Another. You passed on what the wild taught you. Gain Insight or Animal Handling.
True Reputation. Folk began trusting your judgment in the wastes. Gain Scouting or Insight. You may take one Hunter advancement benefit even if the later roll fails. This may be your Pride.
A beast tore you open. Gain one scar and one fear.
You led someone into danger and they did not come back out. Gain one guilty contact or one grieving enemy. This may be your Dark Secret.
Hunger drove you to theft. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
You crossed the wrong forester, clan, or patrol. Gain one rival.
You brought something home that should have stayed in the dark woods. Gain one omen or rumor.
Your prey was no beast at all, or not only that. Your next cycle must change path unless you take one Wear.
Something tracked you back from deep country and found what you loved. Gain one scar, one enemy, and one omen the GM will use later. Your next cycle must change path.
Rank 1 in Master of the Hunt
One hunting contact, guide, or forester ally
One rumor about a beast den, hidden trail, or monster haunt
Bow, arrows, knife, and practical field gear
Traps, skins, and one winter-worthy cloak
One beastwise contact and one hunting rival
D6 silver and one claim on meat, hides, or guiding work
One scar from horn, fang, claw, or weather
One rumor about a lair, legendary beast, or unmarked trail

segments.html: You sang for strangers and ate by their pleasure. The songs are older than you, and crueller, and they will outlast you if you are lucky.
Turn Test: Performance or Manipulation. Normal Skills: Performance, Manipulation, Insight, Lore, Move, Sleight of Hand. Hard-Lesson Skills: Insight, Performance, Manipulation.

segments.text: Minstrel First Turn: Firelight and First Audience

rows: Campfire Song. Folk quieted to hear you. Gain Performance or Lore.
Cheap Inn. You learned how to hold a room full of drunks. Gain Performance or Manipulation.
Borrowed Tale. You stole a story and told it better than its owner. Gain Lore or Insight.
Traveling Troupe. A loose company took you in. Gain Move or Performance. Gain one contact.
Hall Fire. You learned the difference between applause and danger. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Street Performance. Hunger taught you timing and nerve. Gain Performance or Sleight of Hand.

segments.text: Minstrel Second Turn: Patronage and Jealousy

rows: Proud Patron. A hall-lord, shrine-keeper, or rich widow kept you in drink and demanded flattery. Gain Manipulation or Performance.
Sharp Rival. Another singer, poet, or player wanted you humbled. Gain Insight or Performance. Gain one rival.
Love Ballad. You turned somebody's grief into your living. Gain Lore or Manipulation.
Road Dust. You walked from hall to fair to camp with your art on your back. Gain Move or Survival.
Improvised Lie. Your tongue got you out of one danger and into the next. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Strange Audience. Soldiers, outlaws, or cultists paid to hear what decent folk would not. Gain Performance or Scouting.

segments.text: Minstrel Third Turn: Renown or Trouble

rows: Popular Ballad. A song of yours started walking without you. Gain Performance or Lore. This may be your Pride.
Hall Intrigue. Your ears heard more than your mouth should repeat. Gain Insight or Manipulation.
Battlefield Song. You saw men march to death and learned what rhythm does to fear. Gain Performance or Melee.
Mockery. You made the wrong hall-lord, Raven Sister, or chief a laughingstock. Gain Insight or Move. Gain one enemy.
Epic Fragment. You found a half-remembered tale tied to a real ruin or relic. Gain Lore or Scouting. Gain one rumor.
Paid in Kind. Silver was short, so folk paid in food, clothes, gossip, or favors. Gain Manipulation or Sleight of Hand. Roll one silver die.

segments.text: Minstrel Fourth Turn: Last Performance, New Name

rows: Driven Off. Your voice stayed welcome longer than your face. Gain Move or Survival. You must change path next cycle unless a patron keeps you.
Favored Entertainer. A hall or camp became yours for a season. Gain Performance or Manipulation.
Duel of Words. Insults ended in steel, blood, or both. Gain Melee or Insight.
Witness to History. You were present at something others will sing about badly. Gain Lore or Insight.
Broken Heart. Love, vanity, or betrayal drove you back onto the road. Gain Performance or Move. Gain one dark memory.
True Name Won. You gained a name folk remember. Gain Performance or Lore. You may take one Minstrel advancement benefit even if the later roll fails. This may be your Pride.
You slandered the wrong person. Gain one enemy.
Drink, lust, or pride left you in disgrace. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement. This may be your Dark Secret.
Your troupe broke apart violently. Gain one rival or one dead contact's memory.
You stole a song, tale, or lover and paid for it. Gain one scar or one dark secret.
A patron's protection turned to ownership. Your next cycle must change path unless you carry that patron as a burden.
Something you sang woke more than applause. Gain one omen, rumor, or uncanny follower.

A patron, hall, or rival decided your words had cost too much and made certain others agreed. Gain one enemy, lower Standing by 1 in two settlements, and begin play with one dark secret. Your next cycle must change path.
One patron, troupe ally, or hall contact
Instrument, good clothes, and writing kit
One rumor, legend fragment, or map clue learned through song
Instrument, good cloak, and writing tools
D6 silver and one favor owed from a hall, tavern, or camp
One patron contact and one jealous rival
A famous song, insult, or story tied to your name
One scar from a duel, bottle, or bad road
One legend fragment pointing toward a ruin, relic, or feud

segments.html: You carried what folk needed and charged what the road would bear. Every village is hungry for something, and every road collects a toll in sweat or blood.
Turn Test: Manipulation or Insight. Normal Skills: Manipulation, Insight, Crafting, Animal Handling, Scouting, Lore. Hard-Lesson Skills: Insight, Manipulation, Crafting.

segments.text: Peddler First Turn: Cart, Ledger, and Road Dust

rows: Learned the Trade. Someone taught you weights, lies, and patience. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Pack Beast. You learned the worth of calm hands and sound rope. Gain Animal Handling or Move.
Village Fair. Folk bought what they could not grow. Gain Manipulation or Lore.
Thin Profit. You learned how little separates trade from begging. Gain Insight or Survival.
Traveling Stock. You kept goods dry through mud and rain. Gain Crafting or Animal Handling.
Good Eye. You learned what something is worth before its owner does. Gain Insight or Manipulation.

segments.text: Peddler Second Turn: Bargain and Risk

rows: Caravan Work. You moved with others and learned road discipline. Gain Scouting or Animal Handling.
Smuggling Run. Law, priests, or guards made a business opportunity. Gain Scouting or Manipulation.
Bad Debtor. Someone smiled and paid you never. Gain Insight or Melee.
Unexpected Market. You sold to hunters, soldiers, or worse. Gain Manipulation or Lore.
Storm Loss. Weather and water taught you what stock truly matters. Gain Survival or Crafting.
Soft Tongue. You talked your way past danger. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Gain one contact.
Profitable Route. You found a road others feared more than they should. Gain Scouting or Insight. Roll one silver die. This may be your Pride.
Strong Buyer. A hall, shrine, or clan chief began buying from you. Gain Manipulation or Lore.
Escort Trouble. Guards, mercenaries, or robbers made trade expensive. Gain Melee or Insight.
Found Stock. A ruin, corpse, or abandoned cart improved your inventory. Gain Crafting or Scouting.
False Weights. You cheated or were cheated and learned to count twice. Gain Insight or Manipulation. This may be your Dark Secret.
Map in the Margins. A ledger, note, or idle talk gave you a lead worth more than silver. Gain Lore or Scouting. Gain one rumor.

segments.text: Peddler Fourth Turn: Fortune, Debt, or Flight

rows: Ruinous Deal. One bargain broke your purse or your nerves. Gain Insight or Survival. You must change path next cycle unless you stay to rebuild.
Well-Liked Trader. Folk began saving goods for your return. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Dangerous Goods. You carried something worth killing for. Gain Scouting or Move. Gain one enemy or one shadowing rumor.
Good Season. Silver finally stayed in your hand. Gain Manipulation or Animal Handling. Roll 2D6 silver and keep the higher die.
Protected by Favor. A hall-lord, clan, or shrine took interest in your route. Gain Lore or Insight. Gain one contact.
Trader of Repute. Your word began carrying weight. Gain Manipulation or Scouting. You may take one Peddler advancement benefit even if the later roll fails. This may be your Pride.
Robbed on the road. Lose one gear benefit from this cycle and gain one enemy.
You cheated the wrong buyer. Gain one rival.
Debt closed around your throat. Begin play owing silver or service.
Pack animal lost, stolen, or eaten. Gain one bitter memory and one practical shortage.
Rust Brothers, shrine wardens, or hall-lords seized your wares. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
You carried contraband without knowing how far it reached. Your next cycle must change path unless you accept one dangerous patron. This may be your Dark Secret.

A bad route, a dishonest broker, and a creditor with reach undid everything you built. Lose all gear from this cycle, gain one dangerous enemy, and begin play owing a serious named debt. Your next cycle must change path.
Rank 1 in Sharp Tongue or Quartermaster
One caravan, fair-ground, or hall contact
Cart, pack beast, scales, and trade kit
One rumor, map lead, or market secret tied to treasure or danger
Cart or pack beast with basic trade gear
2D6 silver and one debt not yet settled
Scales, ledger, writing kit, and fair-day clothes
One strong trade contact and one jealous rival
One hidden route, fair-ground, or supply source
One rumor about contraband, treasure flow, or a buyer who pays too well

segments.html: You were born to the saddle, or beaten into it. Either way, you learned that a good mount is worth more than a good friend, and more honest.
Turn Test: Animal Handling or Move. Normal Skills: Animal Handling, Move, Melee, Scouting, Marksmanship, Endurance. Hard-Lesson Skills: Move, Animal Handling, Endurance.

segments.text: Rider First Turn: Saddle, Herd, and Open Ground

rows: Learned the Seat. You stopped falling and started listening to the beast. Gain Animal Handling or Move.
Herd Duty. You kept stock moving and alive. Gain Animal Handling or Survival.
Steppe Wind. Distance and weather made your lungs and legs their own. Gain Endurance or Move.
Mounted Errand. You carried word or goods where feet would fail. Gain Scouting or Animal Handling.
Spear Drill. You learned to strike without dismounting. Gain Melee or Marksmanship.
Clan Elder. Someone taught you the price of horse-flesh and pride. Gain Insight or Animal Handling.

segments.text: Rider Second Turn: Speed and Obligation

rows: Hard Ride. One long ride nearly killed beast and rider alike. Gain Endurance or Survival.
Escort Work. You guarded tribute, kin, or rich fools from horseback. Gain Melee or Scouting.
Broken Mount. You learned the cost of fear, injury, or poor hands. Gain Healing or Animal Handling.
Open Competition. You raced or fought for local pride. Gain Move or Marksmanship.
Road Ambush. Riders can be prey as well as hunters. Gain Scouting or Melee.
Good Breeding. You came into a better beast or better tack than before. Gain Animal Handling or Insight.

segments.text: Rider Third Turn: War, Herd, or Renown

rows: War Band. Mounted steel taught you speed and terror together. Gain Melee or Marksmanship. This may be your Pride.
Messenger Ride. You crossed dangerous ground for news that mattered. Gain Move or Scouting.
Horse Trade. You learned the silver side of the saddle. Gain Manipulation or Animal Handling.
Storm Camp. You kept beasts and folk alive through bad weather. Gain Survival or Insight.
Mounted Hunt. Open land and bow work sharpened your eye. Gain Marksmanship or Animal Handling.
Name on the Plain. Folk began to speak of you by mount, speed, or temper. Gain Move or Manipulation. Gain one contact.

segments.text: Rider Fourth Turn: Broken Legs or Hard-Won Place

rows: Fall. Beast, weather, or battle threw you hard. Gain Endurance or Healing. Gain one scar.
Trusted with the Herd. Others put living wealth in your hands. Gain Animal Handling or Insight.
Blood on the Saddle. A raid, feud, or skirmish marked you for good. Gain Melee or Marksmanship. Gain one rival.
Lost Ground. Drought, war, or theft ruined the life you knew. Gain Survival or Move. You must change path next cycle unless you stay to rebuild.
Good Mount. You and one beast became hard to separate. Gain Animal Handling or Move.
Rider of Repute. Your seat and judgment earned respect. Gain Manipulation or Scouting. You may take one Rider advancement benefit even if the later roll fails. This may be your Pride.
Your mount died and took part of you with it. Gain one scar and one grief.
You lost herd, goods, or passengers under your watch. Gain one enemy or one debt. This may be your Dark Secret.
A fall left you wary. Gain one fear tied to speed, height, or hooves.
Clan or employer judged you poorly. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement or camp.
Raiders or soldiers marked your trail. Gain one rival.
Your path is broken by loss of beast, clan, or pasture. Your next cycle must change path unless you take one Wear.
Your mount died badly and those who knew it held you responsible. Gain two scars, lose any mount-related gear from this cycle, and gain one enemy. Your next cycle must change path.
Rank 1 in Pathfinder or Pack Rat
One clan, caravan, or mounted contact
Riding horse with tack and travel gear
One rumor about a road, raid route, hidden pasture, or moving camp
Bow or spear, saddle bags, and field kit
One mounted contact and one bitter rival
D6 silver and one beast-related debt or duty
A branded token, clan knot, or horse charm recognized in some camps
One rumor about raiders, migration, or a fast road to danger

segments.html: You took what was not given to you. Locks, purses, trust, silence — all of it had a price, and you learned to collect before the world noticed. The shadows paid better than honesty, and honesty never kept anyone warm.
Turn Test: Stealth or Sleight of Hand
Normal Skills: Stealth, Sleight of Hand, Scouting, Move, Insight, Melee
Hard-Lesson Skills: Stealth, Sleight of Hand, Move

segments.text: Rogue First Turn: Lookout, Runner, or Cutpurse

rows: Street Lesson. Someone taught you where the knives come from and where the bodies go. Gain Stealth or Insight.
Quick Hands. You found coin in a place someone else thought safe. Gain Sleight of Hand or Move.
Night Roofs. You crossed beams, sheds, and wet shingles in the dark. Gain Move or Scouting.
Knife in the Sleeve. You learned what happens when theft turns to panic. Gain Melee or Stealth.
Bought Silence. Someone paid you not to talk. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Roll one silver die.
Taken In. A gang, crew, or smuggling ring gave you work. Gain Stealth or Sleight of Hand. You also gain one criminal contact.

segments.text: Rogue Second Turn: Heat and Hunger

rows: Guard Sweep. The village, ferry, or camp grew watchful. Gain Scouting or Move.
Bad Fence. You sold to the wrong buyer. Gain Insight or Manipulation. You also gain one rival.
Cold Nights. Hunger and wet straw taught you patience. Gain Survival or Endurance.
Marked Door. You cased a richer house than usual. Gain Scouting or Sleight of Hand.
Work for a Patron. A hall-lord, Raven Sister, or peddler used you quietly. Gain Manipulation or Insight. You also gain one high-born or dangerous contact. This may be your Dark Secret.
Shared Score. A partner saved your skin on the way out. Gain Stealth or Melee. Choose one contact or one future debt.

segments.text: Rogue Third Turn: Big Score or Dirty Fall

rows: Empty Vault. The map was wrong or the treasure already gone. Gain Insight or Survival.
Perfect Entry. For one night every hinge, dog, and drunk slept at the right time. Gain Sleight of Hand or Stealth. This may be your Pride.
Poison Lesson. Someone taught you a quieter way to end trouble. Gain Crafting or Insight. You may treat poison use as part of your later profession history. This may be your Dark Secret.
Cell Door. You spent time behind wood or iron. Gain Endurance or Insight. You also gain one Wear.
Guild Notice. Bigger thieves learned your name. Gain Manipulation or Scouting.
Hidden Cache. You salted coin or tools away where only you could find them. Gain Move or Sleight of Hand. Roll two silver dice and keep both.

segments.text: Rogue Fourth Turn: Betrayal, Escape, or Reinvention

rows: Sold Out. A friend gave you to guards, slavers, or a wronged patron. Gain Insight or Endurance. You must change path next cycle unless you take the traitor as a sworn enemy.
Clean Getaway. You left with enough silver and no one close behind. Gain Move or Scouting. Roll two silver dice.
Blood on the Job. A theft became a killing. Gain Melee or Stealth. You also gain one dark secret.
Under New Name. You vanished and returned as someone else. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Start with one false identity in one settlement.
Shared Blackmail. You learned something worth more than coin. Gain Insight or Manipulation. You also gain one rumor tied to a hall-lord, Raven Sister, or caravan master.

King of Rats. For a short while, everyone below the law answered to you. Gain Stealth or Sleight of Hand. You may take one Rogue advancement benefit even if your advancement roll later fails. This may be your Pride.
Branded, beaten, or maimed in public. Gain one scar and lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
A score went bad and left a corpse behind. Gain one enemy tied to that dead person's kin or patron.
Thrown into a cell. Your next cycle must be Captive, Fighter, Outcast, or Drifter unless you buy your way free through an event.
Your hidden cache was found first. Lose one gear result from this cycle and gain one rival.
You crossed an outlaw chief. Gain one bounty or one gang feud.
Panic taught you caution. Gain Endurance or Insight, then begin play with one fear tied to dogs, prison, heights, or bells in the night.

The wrong score brought the wrong people and they burned more than your plan. Gain one scar, one bounty in one settlement, and lower Standing by 1 in two settlements. Your next cycle must change path.
Rank 1 in Wanderer or Sharp Tongue
Lockpicks, dagger, and a hidden stash of silver
One rumor about a lair, treasure site, or compromising secret
Lockpicks, dagger, and a rolled cloak that hides more than rain
2D6 silver and one person who wants it back
One underworld contact and one jealous rival
A hidden stash in one settlement
A stolen trinket, seal, or letter worth trouble
A map fragment or blackmail secret tied to a ruin, hall, or caravan route

segments.html: You read what should not be read, spoke what should not be spoken, and paid what should not be paid. The world changed for you, and not kindly.
Turn Test: Lore or Insight. Normal Skills: Lore, Insight, Manipulation, Healing, Crafting, Survival. Hard-Lesson Skills: Insight, Lore, Healing.

segments.text: Sorcerer First Turn: Apprentice, Reader, or Dabbler

rows: Dusty Lessons. You read until your eyes burned and your sleep soured. Gain Lore or Insight.
Master's Errand. A teacher trusted you with a dangerous task. Gain Manipulation or Survival.
Hidden Text. You found writing not meant for your hands. Gain Lore or Crafting.
Circle of Salt. You took part in your first true rite and learned fear. Gain Healing or Insight.
Patron's Coin. Someone paid for your studies and expects a return. Gain Manipulation or Lore. Roll one silver die and take one patron contact.
Night Voices. Something answered from the other side of sleep. Gain Insight or Survival. You also gain one occult rumor. This may be your Dark Secret.

segments.text: Sorcerer Second Turn: Experiment and Price

rows: Failed Working. You bled for knowledge and learned caution. Gain Healing or Lore. Add one Wear. This may be your Dark Secret.
Old Bones. A grave, ruin, or cairn yielded secrets. Gain Scouting or Lore.
Court Service. You read omens, soothed nerves, or lied for someone in power. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Poison Shelf. You learned what grows, seeps, and kills. Gain Crafting or Healing.
Forbidden Companion. Another student, ghost, or hidden correspondent traded knowledge with you. Gain Insight or Manipulation. You also gain one occult contact.
Hard Winter. Books do not keep the cold out. Gain Survival or Lore.

segments.text: Sorcerer Third Turn: Recognition or Stain

rows: Symbol Found. A sign, stone, vein, or bloodline called to you. Gain Lore or Insight.
Named as Useful. A hall-lord, cult, or caravan wanted a sorcerer close at hand. Gain Manipulation or Lore.
Blood Cost. You learned power is dearer than silver. Gain Healing or Insight. You also gain one scar or one dark secret.
Buried Artifact. You touched something older than your teacher admitted. Gain Crafting or Lore.
Jealous Eye. Another practitioner marked you as rival or prey. Gain Insight or Manipulation. You also gain one rival.
Whispered Name. People began seeking you for cures, omens, lies, or curses. Gain Manipulation or Healing. Gain +1 Standing in one settlement that fears or needs you. This may be your Pride.

segments.text: Sorcerer Fourth Turn: Break, Exile, or Patronage

rows: Driven Out. Your work frightened the wrong people. Gain Survival or Move. You must change path next cycle unless you stay under a powerful patron's protection.
Arcane Favor. Someone in a hall, shrine, or tower decided your gift was worth the risk. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Gain one patron contact.
Ritual Scar. The rite worked, but not cleanly. Gain Lore or Healing. You also gain one scar touched by sorcery.
Grimoire Fragment. You leave with pages, notes, or signs incomplete but precious. Gain Crafting or Lore.
Haunted Success. You got what you wanted and hate the memory of it. Gain Insight or Manipulation. Add one dark secret.
Master Departed. Your teacher died, vanished, or surrendered the work to you. Gain Lore or Insight. You may take one Sorcerer advancement benefit even if your advancement roll later fails.
Your experiment maimed someone important. Gain one enemy and one fear of discovery.
You were denounced as unclean, cursed, or dangerous. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
Your notes were stolen. Gain one occult rival and lose one gear benefit from this cycle.
A patron demanded more than you can safely give. Begin play owing a service, secret, or relic.
Mishap and backlash left a mark on your flesh. Gain one scar known to those who understand magic.
You saw too much. Gain Insight or Healing, then begin play with one recurring omen, nightmare, or hallucination.
A rite or formula escaped your control and hurt people who had nothing to do with it. Gain one enemy, one visible scar, and one fear tied to the wrong done. Your next cycle must change path.
Rank 1 in Herbalist or Sixth Sense
One occult contact or former mentor
Staff, writing kit, and one useful occult text
One rumor about an artifact, demon site, hidden library, or blood-bound lineage
Staff, writing kit, and a satchel of notes
One occult contact and one occult rival
A grimoire fragment, copied sign, or half-legible formula
D6 silver and one expensive promise owed to a patron
One scar, stain, or visible mark tied to mishap or rite
One rumor about an artifact, demon-haunt, or hidden teacher that the GM may build on later

segments.html: Crisis paths are not professions. They are professionless stretches of time where the character has fallen out of a trade or calling and is struggling to get back on their feet. A cycle spent as a Captive, Drifter, Laborer, or Outcast still teaches skills and still scars the body and the
memory, but it does not advance you toward any profession. These paths exist because life breaks people, and what matters is what they do after.
Any character may enter a crisis path without meeting a threshold.
They took everything — your name, your blade, your say in anything. What they could not take was the part of you that counted the days and kept breathing.

Captive is a crisis path, not a profession. It represents time spent in bondage — as a slave, a prisoner of war, a convicted criminal, a debt-bonded servant, or a hostage held for ransom that never came. Any character may enter it without meeting a threshold. There is no skill to learn here except endurance and the desperate sharpness that captivity breeds. You are not building a life. You are waiting for the chance to reclaim one.
Turn Test: Endurance or Insight. Normal Skills: Endurance, Insight, Survival, Melee, Stealth, Move. Hard-Lesson Skills: Endurance, Might, Insight.

rows: Chains. Iron or rope held you. You learned what hurts less. Gain Endurance or Might.
New Master. They told you the rules with a fist or a switch. Gain Insight or Manipulation.
Stockade Labor. Stone, timber, ditch, or field — the work did not care about your old name. Gain Might or Endurance.
Cage Watch. Days passed in a cell, pit, or wagon. You learned patience or went half-mad. Gain Insight or Survival.
Fellow Prisoner. Someone in the same chains kept you human. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Gain one contact.
Inventory. They took your gear and counted your worth. You counted exits. Gain Scouting or Stealth.

segments.text: Captive Second Turn: Chains and Routine

rows: Heavy Work. The labor grew harder but so did you. Gain Endurance or Crafting.
Guard's Rhythm. You learned when they watched and when they did not. Gain Stealth or Insight.
Beaten. Someone made a lesson of you. You swallowed it and stayed alive. Gain Endurance or Melee.
Small Trade. Scraps, favors, and whispered debts — captives build their own economy. Gain Manipulation or Sleight of Hand.
Tunnel, Crack, or Loose Bar. You found a weakness in the walls. Whether you used it is another matter. Gain Move or Stealth.
Overseer's Trust. Good behavior earned a longer leash. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Gain one contact among captors.
Failed Escape. You ran and were caught. The punishment taught you what failure costs. Gain Move or Endurance.
Someone Died. A fellow prisoner broke, sickened, or was killed. You survived them. Gain Survival or Insight.
Hidden Weapon. You made or stole something sharp and kept it close. Gain Melee or Stealth. This may be your Pride.
Night Whispers. Plans, prayers, or oaths passed between captives after dark. Gain Insight or Manipulation.
Captor's Weakness. You saw a crack in the authority over you — fear, greed, or sentiment. Gain Insight or Manipulation.
Hardened. What once hurt now only aches. Something in you became stone. Gain Endurance or Survival.

segments.text: Captive Fourth Turn: Escape, Release, or Worse

rows: Broke Free. Violence, cunning, or sheer will. You ran and did not stop. Gain Move or Melee. You must change path next cycle.
Ransomed. Someone paid for you. The debt followed. Gain Manipulation or Insight. Gain one debt and one contact.
Released. War ended, sentence served, or the master lost interest. Gain Survival or Endurance.
Sold Onward. New master, new chains, same lesson. Gain Endurance or Insight. You may not change path this cycle unless an event forces it.
Revolt. Captives rose together. Not all survived. Gain Melee or Move. Gain one ally or one dead friend.

Marked But Not Broken. The years took skin and pride but left a core that will not bend. Gain Endurance or Survival. You may take one Captive advancement benefit even if the later roll fails. This may be your Pride.
Scarred by captor — brand, lash-mark, or cut. Gain one visible scar.
Broken limb set badly. One permanent ache remains.
Betrayed by a fellow captive. Gain one enemy within the prison or slave-camp.
Starved or sickened. Lower one physical attribute by 1 (Strength or Agility, your choice).
Witnessed cruelty you cannot forget. Gain one dark memory or one fear. This may be your Dark Secret.
Escaped attempt failed and punishment doubled. Your next cycle must remain Captive unless freed by an event.

They made an example of you that others watched and remembered. Gain two scars and one fear that follows you into every enclosed or watched place. Your next cycle must remain Captive or become Outcast unless freed by a named event.
One contact among former captives or sympathetic guards
One hidden blade, lock-pick, or smuggled tool
One rumor about the captor's weakness, treasure, or secret
Knife, ragged clothes, and nothing else
One fellow survivor as a contact and one captor as an enemy
D6 silver stolen or hidden during captivity
One scar and one oath sworn in chains
One hidden route, tunnel, or weak point in a known stronghold
One rumor about treasure, a captor's secret, or a lost camp

segments.html: No hearth, no master, no plan. The road kept you because nothing else would. That is not freedom — it is what is left when everything else falls away.

Drifter is a crisis path, not a profession. It represents a stretch of rootless, purposeless wandering — time between real lives. Any character may enter it without meeting a threshold. If a forced departure leaves you with no qualifying path, you become a Drifter. You are
not advancing toward anything. You are surviving until something better finds you, or you find it.
Turn Test: Survival or Move. Normal Skills: Survival, Move, Insight, Scouting, Manipulation, Endurance. Hard-Lesson Skills: Survival, Move, Scouting.

segments.text: Drifter First Turn: No Wall, No Master

rows: Road Shelter. You learned where to sleep without dying. Gain Survival or Scouting.
Odd Work. You took whatever labor the day offered. Gain Might or Manipulation.
Quiet Watching. You lasted by seeing trouble early. Gain Insight or Scouting.
Bad Bread. Hunger taught you what pride can be traded for. Gain Endurance or Survival.
Borrowed Name. It was easier not to tell folk the truth. Gain Manipulation or Move.
Fellow Traveler. Someone on the road shared fire, food, or lies. Gain Insight or Survival. Gain one contact.
Mercy Work. Someone paid you in stew and floorboards. Gain Manipulation or Crafting.
Chased Out. One camp, village, or hall turned cold on you. Gain Move or Survival.
Found Shelter. You learned one hidden place from the old Mist years. Gain Scouting or Insight.
Travel Company. You walked with traders, pilgrims, or soldiers for a while. Gain Survival or Lore.
Knife Trouble. Poverty and fear brought steel close. Gain Melee or Endurance.
Road Gossip. The road pays in rumor if not silver. Gain Insight or Manipulation. Gain one rumor.
Crossed Country. You traveled farther than most folk ever do. Gain Move or Scouting. This may be your Pride.
Worked a Season. You stayed in one place just long enough to regret it. Gain Crafting or Might.
Mist Memory. Old fear from the Blood Mist years still clings to roads and ditches. Gain Insight or Survival.
Shared Fire. You became useful to outcasts, widows, hunters, or old men with no sons. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Night Theft. Need pushed your hands before your conscience. Gain Stealth or Sleight of Hand. This may be your Dark Secret.
Weathered. The road thinned you but did not break you. Gain Endurance or Survival.

segments.text: Drifter Fourth Turn: Last Road or New Life

rows: Too Many Doors Closed. The road ran out of kindness. Gain Survival or Melee. You must change path next cycle.
Taken In. A hall, camp, ferry, or caravan finally offered steadier work. Gain Manipulation or Crafting.
Old Enemy Found You. The road is wide until it narrows all at once. Gain Move or Insight. Gain one enemy.
Road Wisdom. You learned which folk lie first and which weather kills fastest. Gain Insight or Scouting.
Quiet Reputation. Some places began treating you as useful instead of rootless. Gain Manipulation or Survival.
Would Not Break. Hard years tempered rather than hollowed you. Gain Endurance or Move. You may take one Drifter advancement benefit even if the later roll fails. This may be your Pride.
Beaten and robbed. Gain one scar and lose one gear benefit from this cycle.
Turned away in winter or storm. Gain one fear or one bitter oath.
Accused of theft, sorcery, or plague-carrying. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
Hunger drove you low. Gain one dark memory or one debt.
Someone kind died after helping you. Gain one grieving contact or one guilty burden.
You can no longer bear the road alone. Your next cycle must change path unless you take one Wear.

The road gave you enemies you never earned and left you with worse than nothing. Gain one scar, one enemy, and lose one gear benefit from this cycle. Your next cycle must change path and begins with one Wear.
One road contact, ferryman, widow, or caravan hand
Blanket roll, knife, and patched but useful travel gear
One rumor about a shelter, ruin, or forgotten way
Blanket, knife, waterskin, and travel kit
One road contact and one place you should not return to
D6 silver hidden in stitching, boot, or belt
One scar and one tale behind it
One hidden shelter or route known only to a few
One rumor about a ruin, ford, or lost company

segments.html: You worked with your hands because no one asked your opinion. The farm, the forge, the yard — they took your strength and gave you calluses in return.

Laborer is a crisis path, not a profession. It represents hard, undifferentiated work — the kind that keeps a body fed but does not build toward a calling. Any character may enter it without meeting a threshold. If a forced departure leaves
you with no qualifying path and the road does not suit you, you become a Laborer. The work is real, the skills are real, but no guild or hall will call this a trade.
Turn Test: Might or Crafting. Normal Skills: Might, Crafting, Endurance, Animal Handling, Insight, Manipulation. Hard-Lesson Skills: Might, Crafting, Endurance.

segments.text: Laborer First Turn: Hands, Tools, and Orders

rows: Field Work. Soil, frost, and strain hardened you. Gain Might or Endurance.
Workshop Chores. Tools taught care before craft. Gain Crafting or Insight.
Stable Labor. Animals make no allowances for weakness. Gain Animal Handling or Might.
Heavy Carry. You learned how much a body can bear before it curses you. Gain Endurance or Move.
Kitchen or Yard. Somebody always needs thankless work done. Gain Crafting or Manipulation.
Master's Eye. Someone noticed you were not useless. Gain Crafting or Might. Gain one contact.

segments.text: Laborer Second Turn: Duty and Exhaustion

rows: Harvest Rush. Work swallowed dawn and dusk alike. Gain Endurance or Animal Handling.
Broken Tool. You learned repair because replacement was impossible. Gain Crafting or Insight.
Poor Pay. The hand that worked hardest did not eat best. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Building Work. Rope, timber, stone, or mud became your world for a while. Gain Crafting or Might.
Sick Beast. Livestock are silver with breath inside them. Gain Animal Handling or Healing.
Shared Burden. Another worker became friend, rival, or both. Gain Insight or Melee.

segments.text: Laborer Third Turn: Skill or Resentment

rows: Trusted with More. Better tools or harder work came your way. Gain Crafting or Endurance. This may be your Pride.
Managed Others. For a while, your hands gave orders instead. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
Winter Repairs. Cold months sharpened useful skill. Gain Crafting or Survival.
Workplace Hurt. Labor bit back with splinter, hoof, stone, or blade. Gain Healing or Endurance. Gain one scar.
Side Trade. You learned to make a little extra under the table. Gain Crafting or Manipulation.
Good Reputation. Someone would ask for you by name when hard work needed doing. Gain Insight or Crafting.

segments.text: Laborer Fourth Turn: Leaving the Yoke

rows: Worked to the Bone. You could not stay in that life another season. Gain Endurance or Might. You must change path next cycle.
Kept It Running. A farm, workshop, or camp held together because of you. Gain Crafting or Animal Handling.
Bad Master. Anger finally outweighed obedience. Gain Melee or Manipulation. Gain one enemy.
Own Tools. You ended with gear that was yours and not borrowed. Gain Crafting or Insight.
Family Duty. Kin need and labor bound you tighter than coin ever did. Gain Insight or Animal Handling. Gain one burden.
Solid Name. Folk began to trust your work without standing over it. Gain Manipulation or Crafting. You may take one Laborer advancement benefit even if the later roll fails. This may be your Pride.
Bad injury on the job. Gain one scar and one fear tied to tool, beast, or height.
Cheated of wages. Begin play owed silver or holding a grudge.
Driven off by a master or kin. Lower Standing by 1 in one settlement.
Hunger and overwork made you cruel or desperate. Gain one dark memory. This may be your Dark Secret.
A beast, wagon, or structure failed under your care. Gain one enemy or one guilty burden.
This life has wrung all it can from you. Your next cycle must change path unless you take one Wear.

A collapse, a violent overseer, or a catastrophic failure marked you and put you out of work at the same time. Gain one scar, one enemy, and lower Standing by 1 in one settlement. Your next cycle must change path.
One employer, craft contact, or farming kin ally
Tool set, practical clothes, and work gear
One rumor tied to stores, hidden tools, cellar caches, or abandoned steadings
Tool kit and sturdy practical gear
Pack beast or work animal, if the story allows it
D6 silver and one unpaid obligation
One employer contact and one bitter former master or rival worker
One scar and one useful lesson behind it
One rumor about an abandoned farm, workshop, cellar, or supply cache

segments.html: You were thrown out, or you fell. It does not matter which. The world outside the firelight is the same for everyone who has no name worth keeping.

Outcast is a crisis path, not a profession. It represents time spent cast out from society — branded, exiled, shunned, or simply forgotten. Any character may enter it without meeting a threshold. Exile, outlawry, branding, disgrace, or the slow death of standing all lead here. You are not building a life. You are enduring the absence of one.
Turn Test: Stealth or Survival. Normal Skills: Stealth, Survival, Scouting, Insight, Move, Melee. Hard-Lesson Skills: Stealth, Survival, Scouting.

rows: Cast Out. You learned quickly what the world charges for solitude. Gain Survival or Insight.
Kept Hidden. Someone sheltered you for reasons of pity, guilt, or profit. Gain Stealth or Manipulation. Gain one contact.
Living Rough. Ditch, hollow, cave, and hedgerow became enough. Gain Survival or Scouting.
Stole to Eat. Shame came second to hunger. Gain Sleight of Hand or Move.
Knife Warning. Loneliness makes poor company and quick steel. Gain Melee or Endurance.
Watched from Afar. You learned settlement life from outside the firelight. Gain Insight or Stealth.
Hunted. Dogs, guards, kin, or debt followed your trail. Gain Move or Scouting.
Bitter Shelter. You stayed with worse folk than yourself because the weather demanded it. Gain Manipulation or Insight.
